title: Be My Travel Muse
content:
"But I must explain to you how all this mistaken idea of denouncing pleasure and praising pain was born and I will give you a complete account of the system, and expound the actual teachings of the great explorer of the truth, the master-builder of human happiness. No one rejects, dislikes, or avoids pleasure itself, because it is pleasure, but because those who do not know how to pursue pleasure rationally encounter consequences that are extremely painful. Nor again is there anyone who loves or pursues or desires to obtain pain of itself, because it is pain, but because occasionally circumstances occur in which toil and pain can procure him some great pleasure. To take a trivial example, which of us ever undertakes laborious physical exercise, except to obtain some advantage from it? But who has any right to find fault with a man who chooses to enjoy a pleasure that has no annoying consequences, or one who avoids a pain that produces no resultant pleasure?"

I met Kristin at Travel Blogging Summit Denver in 2022 and learned a lot from her. She’s the second reason I abandoned all hope with my solo female travel blog: again, she’s got it covered!

Kristin is a former investment banker who realized she wasn’t able to express her creativity and really wanted to write. She quit her job and headed to Bangkok, where she made her dream of living fully from her creative work a reality.

Now she runs Be My Travel Muse and Parenthood Adventures (after having her first child).

Kristin is known as a heavy weight in both the travel blogging and travel writing (i.e. for journalism) worlds.

title: Second Time's the Charm: The Nun II
content:
5 years ago I told y'all how I went to go see The Nun and I did not like it. At. All. What I never updated you on is that over the years, the movie has totally grown on me. While it is not my favorite movie in The Conjuring universe, I enjoy watching it and this created an excitement to see the sequel, The Nun II.

The sequel picks up 4 years after the original movie. Sister Irene is called to save the world again as it has become clear that the demon from the first film still lives on. She is reunited with Maurice in a French boarding school as she learns that the demon has latched itself to him. 

The sequel is full of jump scares and moments where I had to watch through my fingers (the newsstand scene was INTENSE)! However, something that my friends and I have discussed is this plot hole- at the end of the original Nun movie, they attempt to tie Maurice to the Warrens by showing them exorcise him. I believe this should have been left out and saved for this movie. At the end of The Nun II, we see the Warrens receive a call to jump into action. At what point do they exorcise him if he is rescued with Sister Irene's help at the conclusion of this move? Is it me? Am I the drama? Because it just is not adding up to me.

Overall, this movie was such a good time. I loved Storm Reid's character and I would love to see her come back for a third movie.

title: Parenting Blog
content:
No kid acts perfectly at school 100% of the time. Not one. 

So let’s ditch the labels. No more “good kids,” “bad kids,” “troublemakers,” or “bullies.” There’s no need to categorize a child’s behavior.

Why? Because there are a million variables at play, every school year, every day. 

Still, a call from the principal bearing news of behavior problems is concerning. A teacher expressing her frustrations at a parent-teacher conference is upsetting. And seeing the results of a tough day of school on a child’s face is absolutely heartbreaking.

School is a place where kids are learning far more than academics. They’re learning to be respectful, decent schoolmates in a shared environment. Along that path, they’re bound to stumble.

But whether it’s a one-off event or routine trouble, it’s how we handle a child’s school misbehavior that impacts that child’s self-worth and prompts less–or further–misbehavior. That’s why it’s so important to tailor our words and actions towards misbehavior appropriately and strategically.

And, ideally, by getting parents and teachers on the same page.

When school misbehavior occurs, here’s where to start: 

Stay Calm, Empathize, and Find the Root Cause 

When notified about behavior issues at school, some parents understandably jump into defensive mode. You know how great your kids are, and it’s your job to protect them. Any misbehavior at school must be justifiable. 

Did something in the classroom prompt this disruption? 

Is the teacher overreacting? 

Did some other kid start it, and my kid took the fall? 

Other parents might automatically lay full responsibility on their kids, believing there is zero excuse for misbehavior. 

However, the best approach is to gather all the facts before making any assumptions. 

While listening to your child’s side of the story, encourage them to express their feelings and concerns. Assure them you will listen without judgment or blame.

title: 6 Principles of Powerful Storytelling
content:
The purpose of stories is to distract, dispute, and inspire. 

  1. Stories can be used to take a person on a journey within themselves where they can never go by themselves. 
  2. A master storyteller creates a strategic experiential communication that gives people a vision of themselves beyond their mental conditioning and their present circumstances. 
  3. The power of a story is fueled by the energy of who you are behind the words that you speak that create life-changing moments for the listeners. 
  4. The real power of stories lies in their ability to expand the mind, unlock the heart, and ignite the spirit. 
  5. The best stories allow listeners to develop optimism and hope to live out of their imagination instead of locking them in the past within their failures or fears. 
  6. The key to becoming a powerful storyteller is to train with an accomplished coach who has expertise in extracting stories, facilitating transformative shifts, and creating a thirst for a new life while providing value to the audience.

title: CAN I BUY ONE HOUR OF YOUR TIME
content:
A man came home from work late, tired and irritated, to find his 5-year-old son waiting for him at the door.

 

Son: ‘Daddy, may I ask you a question?’

 

Dad: ‘Yeah, sure, what is it?’ replied the man.

 

Son: ‘Daddy, how much do you make an hour?’

 

Dad: ‘That’s none of your business. ‘Why do you ask such a thing?’ The man said angrily.

Son: ‘I just want to know. Please tell me, how much do you make an hour?’

 

Dad: ‘If you must know, I make $50 an hour.’

 

Son: ‘Oh,’ the little boy replied, with his head down.

 

Son: ‘May I please borrow $25?’

The father got angry and said, "If you asked me just to borrow money for a toy or something silly, go to your room and go to bed. "Think about why you are being so selfish. ‘I don’t work hard every day for such childish frivolities.’

 

The little boy quietly went to his room and shut the door.

The man sat down and started to get even angrier about the little boy’s questions. How dare he ask such questions only to get some money?

 

After about an hour or so, the man had calmed down and started to think:

 

Perhaps he had something important to purchase with the $25.00, and he rarely asked for money. The man went to the door of the little boy’s room and opened the door.

‘Are you asleep, son?’ He asked.

‘No, Daddy, I’m awake,’ replied the boy.

 

‘I’ve been thinking, maybe I was too hard on you earlier, said the man. ‘It’s been a long day, and I took out my aggravation on you. Here’s the $25 you asked for.’

The little boy sat straight up, smiling. ‘Oh, thank you, Daddy!’ He yelled. Then, reaching under his pillow, he pulled out some crumpled-up bills.

 

The man saw that the boy already had money and started to get angry again.

 

The little boy slowly counted out his money and then looked up at his father.

 

‘Why do you want more money if you already have some?’ The father grumbled.

 

‘Because I didn’t have enough, but now I do,’ the little boy replied.

 

‘Daddy, I have $50 now. Can I buy an hour of your time? Please come home early tomorrow. I would like to have dinner with you.’

 

PONDER AND CONSIDER

“To be in your children’s memories tomorrow, you have to be in their lives today.” | Barbara Johnson

 

In the Gospel of John, we read that “there is no greater love than this, to give your life to the people you love.” (John 15:13). As I see it, life is time, and time is life. If you want this verse to touch you differently, exchange  the word “life” for “time” and read the verse again:  “There is not greater love than this, to give your time to the people you love.”

 

How are you using the precious gift of time to nurture healthy relationships?

title: GOD WILL PROVIDE
content:
A young woman brings home her fiancé to meet her parents. After dinner, her mother tells her father to find out about the young man. The father invites the fiancé to his study for a drink.

 

“So what are your plans?” the father asks the young man.

 

“I am a bible scholar,” he replies.

“A bible scholar? Hmmm,” the father says. “Admirable, but what will you do to provide a nice house for my daughter to live in, as she’s accustomed to?”

 

“I will study,” the young man replies, “and God will provide for us.”

 

“And how will you buy her a beautiful engagement ring, such as she deserves?” asks the father.

 

“I will concentrate on my studies,” the young man replies. “God will provide for us.”

 

“And children?” asks the father. “How will you support children?”

“Don’t worry, sir, God will provide,” replies the fiancé.

 

The conversation proceeds like this, and each time the father questions him, the young idealist insists that God will provide.

Later, the mother asks, “How did it go, honey?” The father answers, “The bad news is, he has no job and no plans. The good news is he thinks I’m God.”

 

CONSIDER THIS

There’s an old saying that we should “pray as if everything depends on God, work as if everything depends on you.” Some have switched it around: “Pray as if everything depends on you, work as if everything depends on God.”   

 

God is not going to do for us what we can do for ourselves.

title: I STILL RECOGNIZE HER
content:
The husband knew he could not adequately care for his wife, who was in the final stages of Alzheimer’s. He found a compassionate facility and visited her every day.

At noon for lunch.

Not 11:59.

Not 12:01.

Noon. Every day.

Until the day of a minor accident when he found himself in an Emergency Room, his arm being stitched by a nurse as the clock approached the noon hour.

“I need to leave,” he said calmly.

“Hold on,” she told him, “we’re not finished here.”

“But I must visit my wife at noon,” he said.

 

“Well,” she told him gently, “Today you can be a little late.”

The man told the nurse the story of his wife and of the facility where she lives and how when he visits, she does not even recognize him does not know who he is. The nurse patted his hand and said, “That’s okay, hon. You can relax. If she doesn’t even recognize you, there is no harm in being late this one day.”

 

“No,” the man insisted. “I need to go. I need to be there at noon. I know she doesn’t recognize me. But I need to be there because I still recognize her.”

 

 

PONDER AND CONSIDER

  • Real integrity is doing the right thing, knowing that nobody’s going to know whether you did it or not.  Oprah Winfrey
  • Our character is what we do when we think no one is watching. H. Jackson Brown, Jr. 
  • For your pursuit of being the best basketball player possible, you should always assume someone is watching and act accordingly.  John Wooden
  • In your desire to be a high-performing team, you need to give 100% even when no one is.   Cedrick LaFleur
  • How would your behavior change if you were no longer recognized?
  • What would you do if no one was watching?

title: THE DEAF WIFE AND THE CONCERNED HUSBAND
content:
A man feared that his wife wasn’t hearing as well as she used to, and he thought she might need a hearing aid. Not quite sure how to approach her, he called the family doctor to discuss the problem. The doctor told him there was a simple, informal test the husband could perform to give the doctor a better idea about her hearing loss.

 

“Here’s what you do,” said the doctor, “stand about 40 feet away from her, and in a normal conversational speaking tone, see if she hears you. If not, go to 30 feet, then 20 feet, and so on until you get a response.”

 

That evening, the wife was in the kitchen cooking dinner, and he was in the den. He said to himself, “I’m about 40 feet away; let’s see what happens.” Then, in a normal tone, he asked, “Honey, what’s for dinner?” No response.

 

So the husband moved closer to the kitchen, about 30 feet from his wife, and repeated, “Honey, what’s for dinner?” Still no response.

 

Next, he moved into the dining room, where he was about 20 feet from his wife, and asked, “Honey, what’s for dinner?” Again, he gets no response.

 

So, he walked up to the kitchen door, about 10 feet away. “Honey, what’s for dinner?” Again, there is no response.

 

So he walked right up behind her. “Honey, what’s for dinner?” 

“Ralph, for the fifth time I’ve said, chicken!”

 

CONSIDER THIS

The problem may not be with the other one as we always think. It could be very much within us. We sometimes tend to look to heal others’ problems or issues that are actually ours.

title: We Can Do Cancer
content:
Richard was a widower; his wife had suffered a long and painful death from cancer.  Then he met Monica; they came to love each other and each other’s children dearly.

 

Less than a year into their courtship, Monica discovered a lump in her breast.  She had gone to the doctor alone and was alone when she received the devastating news: the lump was malignant.

 

Once the reality set in, her first thought was for Richard and his children.  They had been profoundly wounded by cancer only a few years before.  They were still healing from it.  How could she bring this terrible thing into their lives again?

 

She called Richard immediately and, without telling him why, simply broke off their relationship.  For several weeks, she refused his phone calls and returned his letters.  But Richard would not give up and begged her to see him.

 

Finally, Monica relented and arranged to meet him to say goodbye.  When they met, she could see the deep strain and hurt on his face.  Richard gently asked Monica why she had broken up with him.  Finally, on the verge of tears, she told Richard the truth: that she had found a lump in her breast, that it was malignant, that she had undergone surgery a few weeks before and would begin chemotherapy the following week.

 

“You and the children have lived through this once already,” she told him, “I won’t put you through it again.”

 

He looked at her, his jaw-dropping.  “You have cancer?” he asked.  Reluctantly, she nodded, with tears running down her cheeks.

 

“Oh, Monica,” he said – and began to laugh with relief.  “We can do cancer …  we know how to do cancer.  I thought that you didn’t love me.”

 

Oh, but she did.  And they got through it together, happily married.

 

CONSIDER THIS

Compassion and reconciliation is “fulfilled” every time we act selflessly. Whether we can “do cancer,” whether we know how to comfort and listen and console, whether we can make a soup kitchen or a tutoring program work … whatever gifts and graces we possess can work great and wondrous things when done in the Spirit of the God who came to set us free.

title: We're So Lucky
content:
“Honey, would you drop the kids off at school this morning? I’ve got a lot of shopping to do and errands to run.”

 

“Well, dear, I’ve got a pretty hectic day myself (sigh) …  OK, I’ll do it.  But hurry up, kids!”

 

So Dad and his children jump into the car, and they’re off. The busy father glances at his watch. “Why is traffic so slow this morning? Certainly, people should drive safely, not speed, but this little old man in front of us must be sight-seeing! I’ll pass him as soon as I can… take a shortcut maybe … Oh, no!!”

 

Wouldn’t you know it! The car approaches a railroad crossing just as the lights begin to flash, and the safety gate comes down. Dad’s first thought: “Darn it! We’re going to be held up by a train and be late.”

 

So, as Dad is fuming in the front seat, anxiously tapping his fingers on the steering wheel, reviewing, in his mind, how to make up some time … a sweet, childish voice calls out from the backseat: “Daddy, Daddy, we’re so lucky! We get to watch the train go by!”

 

CONSIDER THIS

Daddy’s take:  an inconvenience, a delay.

Child’s take: the joy of a new experience.

The frustration and the excitement of seeing the train pass by: every occasion could become an adversity if we don’t welcome it as an opportunity for growth and learning.

 

Awareness of the present moment is always a wonderful reminder to stop and enjoy what the journey has to offer along the way. Often the “now,” called by some “the sacrament of the present moment,” is filled with many gifts if we have the eyes to see, the ears to really listen.  In other words, let’s be present.

title: Two Fish Swimming
content:
There were two young fish swimming along and they happened to meet an older fish swimming in the opposite direction, who nodded at them.  The fish says morning boys, how’s the water?  The two fish swim on for a bit and then eventually one young fish turns to another young fish and asks, what the hell is water?

 

The most obvious, important realities are often the ones that are the hardest to see and talk about.

title: Bear, Wolf and Fox parable: Evaluated Experience teaches us a lesson.
content:
One day Bear, Wolf, and Fox went hunting together, after each of them caught a deer they discussed how to divide the spoils.

  • The Bear asked the Wolf how it should be done.
  • The Wolf said everyone should get one deer.
  • Suddenly the Bear ate the Wolf.
  • Then the Bear asked the Fox how he proposed to divide things up.
  • The Fox offered the Bear his deer, then said the Bear should take the Wolf’s deer as well.
  • Where did you get such wisdom asked the Bear?  From the Wolf replied the Fox.

THE POINT:

The school of life offers many difficult courses.  Some we sign up for willingly.  Others we find ourselves taking unexpectedly.  All can teach us valuable lessons, but only if we desire to learn and are willing to reflect on their lessons.

title: Change
content:
The following words were written on the tomb of an Anglican bishop.

 

When I was young and free, my imagination had no limits. I dreamed of changing the world. As I grew older and wiser, I discovered the world would not change, so I shortened my site and I decided to change only my country.

 

But it too seemed immovable. As I grew in my twilight years I settled for changing only my family, those closest to me.

 

But alas, they would have none of it and now as I lie on my death bed, I suddenly realized if I had only changed myself first then by example I would’ve changed my family.

 

And from that inspiration and encouragement, I would have been able to do better for my country.  And who knows I may have even changed the world.

 

Do you want to change the world?

 

Be the change you wish to see in the world. Mahatma Gandhi

title: The Fishermen
content:
A rich industrialist from the north was horrified to find a southern fisherman just leisurely lying in his boat.  Why aren’t you fishing, asked the industrialist.

 

Because I have caught enough fish for the day.

 

Why don’t you catch some more, he asked the fisherman.  What would I do with them, replied the fishermen?

 

You could earn more money, and with that, you could fix the motor of your boat and go into deeper waters and catch more fish. Then you will make enough money to buy nylon nets and these could bring you more fish and more money and soon you could you could have enough money to buy two boats and maybe even a fleet of boats.

 

Then you would be a rich man like me, said the industrialist.  What would I do then, ask the fishermen?

 

Then you could really enjoy life.  Sir, what do you think I’m doing right now, said the fisherman.

 

Moral:

Don’t be quick to judge.

title: The Preacher at Revival
content:
This old Baptist preacher was going to be preaching at a revival and he flew into town and he drove out to the place where the revival was gonna be, in this big open field. This tent was supposed to be filled with hundreds of people, but he didn’t see any cars in the parking lot so he thought, oh well maybe they’re inside anyway.

 

He walks into the tent and there’s nobody there, he ponders and says wow where could everyone be, what happened?

 

He sits down on the first bench and just wakes and finally an old cowboy walks in the tent and sits down next to him.  He said, well thank you for coming there are supposed hundreds of people here but I don’t know where they.

 

I have my sermon all ready but no one to preach to. He asks the cowboy, what do you think I should do?

 

The cowboy says, “Well I’m not a preacher so I can’t tell, but I know this.  If I was going to feed my cattle and only one showed up, I would still at least feed it.”

 

So the preacher jumped all inspired and said you are correct. So made his to the pulpit and preached his sermon to the cowboy.  In fact, he preached and preached for 1.5 hours. Then he finally wrapped it up.

 

Then he went back to sit down next to the cowboy and asked him, well what did you think?

 

Well, the cowboy said, “I’m not a preacher so I really can’t tell, I’m just a cowboy.”  But he said I know this, if I went to feed my cattle and only one showed up, I’d feed it. But I wouldn’t dump the whole load on it.

 

Moral:

#1 You may get inspired to tell your story, but don’t tell your life history in the process.

 

#2 You don’t have to have a full room to deliver your message, to make an impact.

title: The Total picture
content:
You have to get the total picture.

 

It’s like a middle-aged guy who went into a cocktail lounge and went right up to the bartender and asked do you have anything that will cure the hiccups?

 

And without saying a word, the bartender reached down in the bar picked up a real wet bar rag, and just smacked the guy across the face.

 

The guy was stunned and looked at him.  The bartender said, that should do it.

 

Do you have hiccups now? The man said no, but I never had hiccups, my wife’s in the car, she is the one that has them.

 

Moral: As a leader, you must get the total picture before you act or respond.

title: Things that sound good but never happened.
content:
Just like the guy who was introduced to speak at a conference, they were told as an audience that this man made a $10 million profit in the stock market in New York and he was going to talk about it.

 

And so when the man stood up, he said I want to make a few corrections it really wasn’t $10 million it was $20 million.

 

It really wasn’t dollars it was pounds.

 

It wasn’t in New York it was in London.

 

It wasn’t me it was my brother.

 

And it wasn’t made it was lost.

 

Things that sound good but never really happened. Are you with me?

title: Two Guys Hunting
content:
• A couple of guys were hunting
  • One of them fell to the ground and appeared not to be breathing, and his eyes were rolled back in his head.
  • His friend pulls out his cell phone to call 911. He tells her my friend is dead; what should I do?
  • The operator calmly replies, calm down, I can help you. Let's first make sure he is not breathing. First, there is silence, and then she hears a gunshot.
  • He comes back to the phone and says, ok, now what?
  • As this story illustrates, we can hear what is being said without listening to what is being communicated.
  • The hunter heard what the operator told him and technically did make sure his hunting companion was dead. If he had been listening, though, I don't think he would have shot his partner.

 

The Point:

The message here is that when we hear without really listening, our leadership is bound to suffer, and so will our followers.

title: 4 guys were in a boat
content:
Four guys were in a boat,

On one end of the boat were two guys trying to get water out of the boat and get the hole patched up.  One of the other guys on the other end of the boat was looking at them and said, “Boy, I’m glad that hole is not on our end of the boat.”

 

POINT

  1. I want you to know that we are in the boat together, and if one of us goes down, we all go down.
  2. I want you to know that we are all in the boat together, and if one of us wins, we all win.
  3. There is no “your department vs my department.”  They are all our departments.

title: 4 minute Mile
content:
A great example of this is the late Roger Bannister, the first man in history to run a mile in under four minutes. Up to then, many people widely believed that such a feat was impossible, that human beings simply could not run that fast. Some even believed someone’s heart could explode from the effort! Roger Bannister didn’t listen. He chose to follow his own beliefs and reject the other voices.

 

Then, on May 6, 1954, Bannister made history by completing the mile in 3:59.4 minutes. And guess what? It didn't kill him. His belief that he could do it enabled him to overcome the naysayers and “experts” who said it couldn’t be done. That’s not all, though.

 

Six weeks later, someone else broke Bannister’s record. No one had ever broken the four-minute mile before, but now two different people had done it within weeks of each other. Today, more than sixty years later, the one-mile record has dropped all the way down to 3:43. All it took was one man saying, “I can do this. I will do this.” Once he proved it was possible, others embraced the possibility for themselves and made it happen.

 

And, by the way, when you get there, don’t apologize for winning. Don’t feel bad about your success; enjoy it! Too many people are afraid of building wealth/ultra-success. They act like they don’t deserve it and feel guilty for achieving more than someone else.

 

Bannister’s attitude and actions are compounded when exposed to others. His attitude spread. Today, every world-class runner who competes at that distance can run a mile in less than four minutes. Attitudes are contagious!

 

LESSON:

  • Don’t believe the lie that you can’t do something, anything.
  • What is your self-limiting belief?
  • A scarcity mindset will always tell you that you can’t do it. DON’T BELIEVE IT

title: 400-pound man
content:
A big, heavy guy, about 400 lbs, goes up to a sidewalk scale with one of those big needles on it. It was broken, but he didn’t know it was broken.  He puts a quarter in, steps on the scale, and the needle goes to 60 lbs and stops.  A kid is standing with his mother right beside him, and he sees what’s happening. He looks at this big guy and looks at the 60 lbs, and he is trying to figure out what just happened. Finally, his face lights up, and he says, hey, Mom, that man’s hollow.

 

The Lesson:

You cannot give what you do not have.  If you are going to enlarge people, you must enlarge yourself.

title: A bricklayer tried to move about 500 lbs of brick
content:
A bricklayer tried to move about 500 lbs of brick from the top of a 4-story building to the sidewalk below.  The problem was that he tried to do it alone.  This is his own story, taken from his insurance claim form.

 

It would have taken too long to carry bricks down by hand, so I loaded them in a barrow and lowered them by a pulley, which I had fastened to the top of the building.  After tying the rope securely at ground level, I then went up to the top of the building; I fastened the rope around the barrel, loaded it with bricks, and swung it out over the sidewalk for the descent.  Then I went down to the sidewalk, and I untied the rope, holding it securely to guide the barrel down slowly.  But since I weighed only 140 lbs, the 500 lb load jerked me from the ground so fast that I didn’t have time to think and let go of the rope.

 

And as I passed between the 2nd and 3rd floor, I met the barrel coming down.  This accounts for the bruises and lacerations on my upper body.

 

I held tightly to the rope until I reached the top where my hand became jammed in the pulley.  This accounts for my broken thumb.

 

At the same time however, the barrel hit the sidewalk with a bang and the bottom fell out.  With the weight of the bricks gone, the barrel weighed only 40 lbs.  Thus my 140 lb body began a swift descent and I met the empty barrel coming up, this accounts for my broken ankle.

 

Slowed only slightly, I continued the descent and I landed on the pile of bricks, this accounts for my sprained back and broken collarbone.  At this point, (I love this statement) I lost my presence of mind completely and I let go of the rope.  And the empty barrel came crashing down on me, this accounts for my head injury.

 

And as for the last question on your insurance claim form, “What would you do if the same situation arose again?” Please be advised that I’m finished trying to do the job all by myself.

 

Now this is what happens when you try to do it all by yourself. Law of significance states, one is too small a number to achieve greatness.

title: A Dish of Ice Cream
content:
In the days when an ice cream sundae cost much less, a 10-year-old boy entered a hotel coffee shop and sat at a table. A waitress put a glass of water in front of him.

 

“How much is an ice cream sundae?”

 

“50 cents,” replied the waitress.

 

The little boy pulled his hand out of his pocket and studied a number of coins in it.

 

“How much is a dish of plain ice cream?” he inquired. Some people were now waiting for a table, and the waitress was a bit impatient.

 

“35 cents,” she said brusquely.

 

The little boy again counted the coins. “I’ll have the plain ice cream,” he said.

The waitress brought the ice cream, put the bill on the table, and walked away. The boy finished the ice cream, paid the cashier, and departed.

 

When the waitress came back, she began wiping down the table and then swallowed hard at what she saw.

 

There, placed neatly beside the empty dish, were 15 cents – her tip.


 

Moral:

Your perspective changes when you have more information, and it should cause a transformation in your thoughts and actions.

title: A dispassionate young man approached Socrates
content:
A dispassionate young man approached this successful business leader with a question.  He said I’ve come to you to get advice on success.

 

The business leader told the young man to meet him down at the river, and when the young man arrived, he noticed the business was in the water.  The business leader instructed the young man to meet him in the water.  Once he got in the water, the business leader dunked him for 30 seconds and then asked him what he wanted.  The young man repeated, “I want your advice on success.”  The business leader dunked him again, this time for a little longer.  Then asked what do you want, the young man replied, “Air, I want air.”   

 

Good, answered the Business leader. “Now, when you want advice on success as much as you want air, you shall have it.”

 

The Lesson:

There is no substitute for passion.  It is fuel for the will.  If you want anything badly enough, you can find the willpower to achieve it.

title: A family that wanted its family history
content:
A family wanted its family history written up so they hired a biographer to do this, but they were worried about how to handle the family’s black sheep Uncle George, who had been electrocuted in the electric chair for murder.  

No problem, said the biographer, “I’ll just say that Uncle George occupied the chair of applied electronics, at an important government institution.  He was attached to his position by the strongest of ties, and his death came as a real shock.

title: A grandpa and grandma who visited their grandchildren
content:
A grandpa and grandma were visiting their grandchildren. Each afternoon, Grandpa would lie down for a nap. One day, as a practical joke, the kids decided to put Limburger cheese in his mustache. Quite soon, he awoke sniffing. “Lord, this room stinks,” he exclaimed as he got up and went out into the kitchen.

 

He wasn’t there long until he decided that the kitchen smelled, too, so he walked outdoors for a breath of fresh air. Much to Grandpa’s surprise, the open air brought no relief, and he proclaimed, “The whole world stinks!”

 

The Lesson:

How true is this in life? When we carry “Limburger cheese” in our attitudes, the whole world smells bad. We are individually responsible for our view of life.

title: A husband was on his deathbed
content:
A husband was on his death bed and he told his wife I have $50,000 in my account and I want to be buried with all of my money.

 

His wife said “ok.”

 

A few days later, he died. Right before they closed the casket, his wife walked up to the casket with a little wooden box and put it in his casket. Her friend asked you didn’t put $50,000 in the casket, did you?  She replied, yes, I did. I’m a Christian, I cannot lie.

 

Her friend asked, are you crazy to bury $50k? She replied, no.

I wrote a check.

title: A man started a company
content:
A man started a company and built it into a very large enterprise, and was planning to hand over the reins to his son at retirement.  One day, he was walking through the factory and observed his son angrily berating an employee in front of other employees.  He looked at his son and motioned for him to come to his office.

 

David, he began.  I wear two hats around here.  I am the boss and I am your father.  Right now, I am going to put my boss’s hat on.  You’re fired.  You are done here.  I will not have that kind of behavior in my company and will not ever tolerate employees being treated that way.  I have warned you about this kind of thing before, and you are still doing it.  So, I have to let you go.

 

Then he said, Now, I am going to put on my father’s hat.

After a moment’s pause, he continued.  Son, I heard you just lost your job.  How can I help you?

 

  • Emotionally strong people honor their relationships while at the same time guarding against letting others control them, especially in difficult relationships.

title: A man was looking for a parking spot
content:
A man was looking for a parking spot, so he prayed, “Please God help me find a parking spot, please help me find a parking spot.”

Then he sees an open parking spot, so he says never mind, I found one.

title: A Pound of Butter
content:
There was a farmer who sold a pound of butter to a baker. One day the baker decided to weigh the butter to see if he was getting the right amount, which he wasn’t. Angry about this, he took the farmer to court.

 

The judge asked the farmer if he was using any measure to weigh the butter. The farmer replied, “Your Honor, I am primitive. I don’t have a proper measure, but I do have a scale.”

 

The judge asked, “Then how do you weigh the butter?”

 

The farmer replied,

“Your Honor, long before the baker started buying butter from me, I have been buying a pound loaf of bread from him. Every day when the baker brings the bread, I put it on the scale and give him the same weight in butter. If anyone is to be blamed, it is the baker.”

 

Moral of the story:

In life, you get what you give. Don’t try and cheat others.

title: A turkey and his BS
content:
A turkey was chatting with a bull. “I would love to be able to get to the top of that tree,” sighed the turkey, “but I haven’t got the energy.”

 

“Well,” replied the bull, “why don’t you nibble on some of my droppings? They’re packed with nutrients.”

 

The turkey pecked at a lump of bull droppings and found that it actually gave him enough strength to reach the lowest branch of the tree. The next day, after eating some more of the bull droppings, he reached the second branch. Finally after a fourth night, there he was proudly perched at the top of the tree. But he was promptly spotted by a hunter, who shot him down out of the tree.

 

The moral of the story: BS might get you to the top, but it won’t keep you there.

title: A Very Special Bank Account
content:
Imagine you had a bank account that deposited $86,400 each morning. The account carries over no balance from day to day, allows you to keep no cash balance, and every evening cancels whatever part of the amount you had failed to use during the day. What would you do? Draw out every dollar each day!

 

We all have such a bank. Its name is Time. Every morning, it credits you with 86,400 seconds. Every night is written off, as a loss, whatever time you have failed to use wisely. It carries over no balance from day to day. It allows no overdraft so you can’t borrow against yourself or use more time than you have. Each day, the account starts fresh. Each night, it destroys any unused time. If you fail to use the day’s deposits, it’s your loss and you can’t appeal to get it back.

 

The Lesson:

There is never any borrowing time. You can’t take a loan out on your time or against someone else’s. The time you have is the time you have and that is that. Time management is yours to decide how you spend the time, just as with money you decide how you spend the money. It is never the case of us not having enough time to do things, but the case of whether we want to do them and where they fall in our priorities.

title: A woman accompanied her husband
content:
A woman accompanied her husband to the doctor, after the checkup the doctor told his wife secretly.

If you don’t do the following your husband will surely die.

 

Each morning send him off to work with a really good breakfast so he is in a really good mood.

 

For lunch, make him a very nutritious meal, so he is in a good frame of mind as he goes back to work.

 

For dinner, fix him a really good meal, and don’t burden him with any household chores.  Satisfy his every whim.

 

On the way home, the husband asked his wife what the doctor said to her.  She looked at him and said you are going to die.

title: Adversity and overcoming
content:
Adversity and overcoming

On July 30, 1945, the USS Indianapolis was sunk by a Japanese submarine.

The ship was in the South Pacific close to the Philippines, toward the back end of World War II.

 

900 of the 1200 men on board survived and are in the water.

 

In the midst of the chaos of the man on fire and burning in the water and leader was needed. Men were screaming, scared, and confused. It was a little after midnight. Captain Park jumped in charge and tried to engage the men by having them number themselves.

 

In the midst of chaos, a leader is always needed, and he took charge. SOS went out but no one from the Navy took action on it to come and rescue them. So, the men were on their own. Now the men are still in the water for a few hours later, and sharks start to arrive and start picking off the men; all you hear are screams of confusion.

 

Captain McVeigh who is the man in charge of the ship was separated from the rest of the crew.

Some of the men became confused and delusional in the heat and the saltwater, so they ended up dying. Others were so confused that they wanted to die.

 

“The easiest thing to do when failure is close at hand is to quit”. A few of the soldiers even commented they would have rather die than continue to live in those conditions.

 

By day three, 400 of the 900 people who jumped off the ship had died. By the same day, no one from the Navy still knew that they were missing. When they didn’t arrive in the Philippines, the people in the harbor just assumed that they were sent on another mission so they took the ship’s name off the board.

 

Captain Park started swimming in between the men to help maintain order and morale. He was doing everything he could to make sure that the men were taken care of. By the end of day three, Captain Park disappeared to the ocean floor. By the end of the third night, another hundred men died.

 

By day four only about 350 of the total 1200 men are still alive. Then suddenly a plane flying at 3000 feet doing a routine tour looking for submarines notices a black oil slick in the water and notices people in the water. Then enters one single thought into the mind of the men who saw the plane, I WILL SURVIVE.

 

What would you do in that situation, struggle to survive, or give up?

 

Finally, around the end of day 4 brought a massive rescue attempt. Some had to wait until Day five, including Captain McVay.

879 were killed.

317 survived.

Captain McVeigh was court-martialed for inefficiency on the ship. Some 20 years later still feeling guilt and he walked out to his front yard put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger.

 

The Lesson:

No man aboard that ship that survived was left unchanged. What happened in the midst of this tragedy is teamwork, leaders stepped up and influence.  Also notice how he stood with each man through this ordeal.

title: After winning his 3rd world championship
content:
After winning his 3rd world championship, Bull Rider Tuff Hedeman didn’t have a big celebration.  He moved on to Denver to start the new season and the whole process over again.  His comment: “The bull won’t remember what I did last week.”  

The Lesson:

Whether you’re an untested rookie or a successful veteran, if you want to be a champion tomorrow, be teachable today.

title: After WWII a young lieutenant and his General
content:
After WWII a young lieutenant and his General were on a train and when they got on there were only 2 seats left, they were sitting across from a beautiful young lady and her grandmother.   So, they sat facing them.  As their train went out, it went through a long tunnel.

 

For about 10 seconds there was a moment of darkness and in the silence of the moment, those on the train heard 2 things a kiss and a slap.  Everyone on the train had their own perception of what happened.

 

  • The young lady thought to herself, I’m flattered that the young lieutenant kissed me.  But I’m embarrassed that my grandmother hit him.
  • The grandmother thought I was aggravated that he kissed my granddaughter but I’m proud she had the courage to retaliate.
  • The General thought my lieutenant showed a lot of guts kissing that girl, but why did she slap me by mistake?
  • The lieutenant is the only one on the train that knows what happened.  You see, in that brief moment, he had the opportunity to kiss a pretty girl and slap his general at the same time.

 

The Lesson:

The most common thing that blindspot leaders have is a singular perspective.

title: Alabama Coach Paul “Bear” Bryant
content:
• Alabama was ahead by 6 points with seconds to go against Auburn,  Coach Bear Bryant told 2nd string QB to play it safe and run the clock out.
  • The QB decided to pass it on 4th down. He dropped back to pass but a world-class sprinter safety intercepted and started running it back.
  • The QB chased him down at the 2-yard line as time ran out.
  • The opposing coach asked Bear Bryant, what's this talk that your QB can't run?
  • Bear Bryant stated, “Your man was running for 6 points, my QB was running for his life".

 

  • *Joseph's story is another story of overcoming and making the best of a bad situation. His brothers sold him into slavery, he was imprisoned, and he was a servant. Yet he rose to the top of all situations and became a leader of people including his own brothers. But he held no bitterness.

 

Law of Consistency: Motivation gets you going, and discipline keeps you going and growing.

The Law of the Big Picture: The goal is more important than the role.

title: Alabama football
content:
The great football coaches are not the ones with a great plan, because they all have plans.  The great ones know how to make halftime adjustments.

 

Just ask Nick Saban about it.  In the 2018 college national championship game, he pulled his starting QB Jalen Hurt(who had taken them to two championship games before) for backup Tua.  You see, Nick knew that they were good but to be at their best in the 2nd half he needed to make a change. Without that change, Georgia wins the national championship game.

 

Then 1 year later in the SEC Championship game(2019), the same 2 QBs, this time he called up Jalen Hurt in the 2nd half to help lead them to the championship when Tua got hurt.  After the game, they ask Nick, what he thought when he had to put Jalen in.  He said, “Jalen is a champion and he knows how to win, so I was totally confident in putting Jalen in.”

 

The Lesson:

Leaders know how and when to make adjustments to help the team win.

Never accept good when great is available.

 

The Law of Victory: Leaders find a win for their team to win.

title: As I went back home for a reunion
content:
As I went back home for a reunion, I ran into an old friend, Raymond.  I said hello Raymond how are you doing?  He said, oh I’m doing great.  I asked him how is the ministry going?  He replied, “Oh I’m no longer a minister, I’m a funeral director now.”

 

I was surprised because I knew he always wanted to be a minister like his father.  So I asked why he made the transition.  He replied, “That was simple, when I was a pastor, I’d bring them in for counseling and try to straighten them out, but it just wouldn’t work.  They would always go back out and do some stupid stuff.  He said, what I love about my job now, is when I straighten them out, they stay straight.”

 

I learned a long time ago, that it’s easy working on dead people, it’s the live ones are always moving on you.

title: Ask more questions
content:
A mother said to her daughter, stop asking so many questions.  She said curiosity killed the cat.  Well, the little girl was puzzled, so she asked her mother, what did the cat want to know?

 

Questions don’t hurt you, they help you thrive.

 

Strategic thinking is important.

title: Bank Loan: Fencing In or Out?
content:
A farming community banker said here is how he determines if he will approve or deny a farming loan.

 

When a farmer comes in, he would ask them one question: Are you fencing in or fencing out?

 

He said if a farmer is fencing in, he is trying to secure what he has.   And he has no plans on growing or developing. He is just trying to hold on to what he has.  He said, I seldom approve loans for someone who is trying to hold on.

 

He said if they are fencing out, I almost always loan them money.  They are going to buy some more land, some more livestock, and put some more fences up.  If you are fencing out, there is potential for profit there. If you are fencing in, you are at best, worrying about just holding on.


The Point:

If you are Maintaining, you are a fencing in person.

If you are Creating, you are a fencing out person.

title: Benefits of Failure
content:
This is a parable on the benefits of failure.

 

The ceramics teacher announced on opening day that he was dividing the class into two groups. All those on the left side of the studio, he said, would be graded solely on the quantity of work they produced, all those on the right solely on its quality.

 

His procedure was simple: on the final day of class he would bring in his bathroom scale and weigh the work of the “quantity” group: fifty pounds of pots rated an “A,” forty pounds a “B,” and so on. Those being graded on “quality,” however, needed to produce only one pot—albeit a perfect one—to get an “A.”

 

Well, come grading time a curious fact emerged: the works of the highest quality were all produced by the group being graded for quantity. It seems that while the “quantity” group was busily churning out piles of work—and learning from their mistakes—the “quality” group had sat theorizing about perfection, and in the end had little more to show for their efforts than grandiose theories and a pile of dead clay.

 

The Lesson:

It doesn’t matter whether your objectives are in the area of art, business, ministry, sports, or relationships. The only way you can get ahead is to fail early, fail often, and fail forward.

title: Blame Game (Explanations given to insurance companies why people had an accident)
content:
Blame Game (Explanations given to insurance companies why people had an accident)

Accountability

 

  1. As I reached an intersection a hedge sprang up blocking my vision.
    • You know how those bushes just pop up out of nowhere?

 

  1. The telephone post was approaching fast when I tried to swerve out of its path it struck my front end.
    • Those moving telephone poles will get you every time.  I just hate that.

 

  1. I had been driving my car for 4 years when I fell asleep and had an accident.
    • Well, I guess, if you had been driving for 4 years it was time to go to sleep.

 

  1. I was on the way to the doctor’s office with rear-end trouble when my universal joint gave way causing me to have an accident.

 

  1. I was coming home, I pulled into the wrong driveway and hit a tree I did not have.
    • Yeah, that will do it every time.

 

  1. The pedestrian had no idea which way to run so I ran over him.
    • So, if you are indecisive you getting run over.

title: Bologna Story
content:
Two guys having lunch, had been working in the factory all day.  One guy pulls out his lunch pale, opens it up, pulls out the sandwich, and finds it’s a bologna sandwich.  He is ticked.  He looked at his buddy and said I have a bologna sandwich again today, this is the 3rd time this week I have had a bologna sandwich.  He says I hate bologna sandwiches.

 

Why is it that every day I reach in my lunch pail I have a bologna sandwich, I don’t like bologna, I hate bologna, and I don’t want another bologna sandwich.  His friend says, relax, take a chill pill, it’s ok.  Just tell your wife you don’t like bologna sandwiches and you don’t want that anymore.  He said, keep my wife out of this, I fix my own lunch.  I fix my own lunch.

 

Most of the bologna we have in our life, we packed in our own pale.

 

The question is:

  1. What bologna are you packing in your own pale?
  2. What bologna are you cooking up in your life every day?
  3. What bologna are you thinking into your life consistently?

 

We are the reason for the burdens we carry in our lives.

title: Box Full of Kisses
content:
Some time ago, a man punished his 3-year-old daughter for wasting a roll of gold wrapping paper. Money was tight and he became infuriated when the child tried to decorate a box to put under the Christmas tree.

 

Nevertheless, the little girl brought the gift to her father the next morning and said, “This is for you, Daddy.”

 

The man became embarrassed by his overreaction earlier, but his rage continued when he saw that the box was empty. He yelled at her; “Don’t you know, when you give someone a present, there is supposed to be something inside?”

 

The little girl looked up at him with tears in her eyes and cried;

 

“Oh, Daddy, it’s not empty at all. I blew kisses into the box. They’re all for you, Daddy.”

 

The father was crushed. He put his arms around his little girl, and he begged for her forgiveness.

Only a short time later, an accident took the life of the child.

 

Her father kept the gold box by his bed for many years and, whenever he was discouraged, he would take out an imaginary kiss and remember the love of the child who had put it there.

 

Moral of the story:

Love is the most precious gift in the world.  As a leader, you must learn how to control your emotions, feelings, and words because once they are out, it’s hard to pull them back.

title: Boxer Gene Tunney won the world heavyweight
content:
Boxer Gene Tunney won the world heavyweight championship by beating Jack Dempsey.  Most people don’t know that when Tunney started his boxing career, he was a power puncher.  But before turning pro, he broke both hands.  His doctor and manager told him he would never be a world champion as a result.  But that didn’t deter him.

 

“If I can’t become a champion as  a puncher,” he said, “I’ll make it as a boxer.”  He learned and he became one of the most skillful boxers ever to become champion.

 

The Lesson:

Never allow others to put obstacles in the pathway to your dreams.

title: Calhoun
content:
It’s hard to drop the ball if you never carry the ball.  Some people don’t want to carry the ball, because they want to be able to say, I didn’t mess up.

Two HS teams went to the championship and one of the teams thought they would win for sure because they had this great runner named Calhoun.  This was a major game, it was for all the marbles.

Much to the surprise of Calhoun, the entire 1Q he never ran the ball, never touched it.  It was a defensive battle.

The score was 0-0 and by halftime, it was still tied. In fact, the whole conversation at halftime was that Calhoun had not run the ball yet.

By 3Q, the people started yelling “Give Calhoun the ball.” At the end of the 3Q score was still tied 0-0, and players were still being carried off the field.

Finally, in the 4Q, everybody was yelling “Give Calhoun the ball,” and “Give Calhoun the ball.”  Calhoun comes out of the huddle, looks up at the crowd, and yells Calhoun doesn’t want the ball.

 

2nd part of the story

The old Pope joke.  The Pope was sick and needed a heart transplant.  Everybody wanted the Pope to get a new heart. So finally the Pope said, I’m gonna blow this feather, and whomever it lands on, will have to give me their heart.  The people were excited and said, “Drop the feather, drop the feather.”  Then when the feather started falling and got close by, people started blowing it away from them.

There are individuals like Calhoun and the people, who want to be on the team but don’t want to commit to the entire thing.

title: Carrie Rich: The Give Up
content:
In her 20s, Carrie Rich worked as a senior director at Inova Health Systems in Virginia. She wanted her life to make a difference. She told her boss that she planned to solicit donations from her friends, family, and colleagues to help people in need. Her boss gave Rich $100 to get started. Her goal was to turn that $100 into $1,000 donations each for six different organizations that help people around the world.

 

To accomplish this goal, starting in 2011, Rich wrote to everyone she knew and to people she didn’t know to ask for money to assist in her charity, which she named The Global Good Fund. Money started to roll in. Rich’s small fund grew to $6,052 in two weeks. Soon after, a casual acquaintance donated $1 million to help Rich’s good work. In 2012, Rich quit her job to work full-time to build her new philanthropic organization.

 

“The people who most often make the biggest difference are the people who are first to step up and help.”

 

Like many other ordinary people who make the world a better place, Rich started out small – the first step on her important journey – and built up from there. Specifically, she took $100 and – with intention – built it to more than $1 million. She now devotes her life on a full-time basis to helping needy people. Now, impoverished people all over the world benefit from her intentionality.

 

“One of the great ironies of life is that if you give up your life, you gain it. If you help others, you benefit. If you lose yourself, you find yourself.”

title: Charlie Brown was in the backyard
content:
Charlie Brown was in the backyard doing target practice with his bow and arrow.  He shoots the arrow into the fence, and wherever the arrow sticks, he uses his crayon to draw his target.  Then he pulls back and lets the arrow fly, and where it lands is another target.

 

Well, here comes Lucy, the momentum breaker.  She looks at what he is doing and says, Charlie, that is not the way you do target practice.  He says, I know, but if you do it my way, you never miss.

 

The Lesson:

Get outside your Comfort Zone

Be willing to do things differently / take risks.

Growth is the only guarantee that tomorrow will be better than today.

title: Chinese bamboo tree takes 5 years
content:
Chinese bamboo tree takes 5 years to pop above the surface, then once it pops up you can visually see it growing.  But you have to water and fertilize for all that time. In fact, in 5 weeks, once it is above the surface, it can grow up to 90 feet tall.  Personal growth works similarly; it works behind the scenes. YOU MAY NOT SEE EVIDENCE OF IT for a while because it is growing inside of you.

 

But you have to keep fertilizing and watering, and then one day, all of a sudden, it will show unbelievable growth.  However, your friends colleagues, and family members may ridicule you; they may laugh at it and tease that nothing has changed.  You see, some of them quit on their dream, and some of them gave up on their goals, but if you keep going, you will be like that bamboo tree.

 

You will shoot up in the sky:

  1. Your scores get better
  2. Your overall performance improves
  3. You start to think differently
  4. You start to walk differently
  5. Your mindset changes
  6. Your bank account changes
  7. Your friends change
  8. You realize your dreams

 

I challenge you to put your dream to the test.

title: Chippie the parakeet
content:
Chippie the parakeet, never saw it coming. One second he was peacefully perched in his cage. The next, he was sucked in, washed up, and blown over.

 

The problems began when Chippie's owner decided to clean Chippie's cage with a vacuum cleaner. She removed the attachment from the end of the hose and stuck it in the cage. The phone rang, and she turned to pick it up. She'd barely said "hello" when "ssssopp!" Chippie got sucked in.

 

The bird owner gasped, put down the phone, turned off the vacuum, and opened the bag. There was Chippie -- still alive but stunned.

 

Since the bird was covered with dust and soot, she grabbed him and raced to the bathroom, turned on the faucet, and held Chippie under the running water. Then, realizing that Chippie was soaked and shivering, she did what any compassionate bird owner would do . . . she reached for the hair dryer and blasted the pet with hot air.

 

Poor Chippie never knew what hit him.

A few days after the trauma, the reporter who'd initially written about the event contacted Chippie's owner to see how the bird was recovering. "Well," she replied, "Chippie doesn't sing much anymore -- he just sits and stares."

 

It's hard not to see why. Sucked in, washed up, and blown over . . . That's enough to steal the song from the stoutest heart.---Max Lucado, In the Eye of the Storm, Word Publishing, 1991, p. 11.

 

The Lesson:

What we learn from this bird drama is that when leaders suck in, wash up and blow over their people, they will be stunned, silent and have nothing to say.  In other words, all their innovative ideas and creative thoughts have been sucked in the vacuum.  Leaders should help their teams sing, thrive and grow.

title: Colonel Sanders | Kentucky Fried Chicken
content:
Once, there was an older man, who was broke, living in a tiny house, and owned a beat-up car. He was living off of $99 social security checks. At 65 years of age, he decided things had to change. So he thought about what he had to offer. His friends raved about his chicken recipe. He decided that this was his best shot at making a change.

 

He left Kentucky and traveled to different states to try to sell his recipe. He told restaurant owners that he had a mouthwatering chicken recipe. He offered the recipe to them for free, just asking for a small percentage of the items sold. Sounds like a good deal, right?

 

Unfortunately, not so for most of the restaurants. He heard NO over 1000 times. Even after all of those rejections, he didn’t give up. He believed his chicken recipe was something special. He got rejected 1009 times before he heard his first yes.

With that one success Colonel Hartland Sanders changed the way Americans eat chicken. Kentucky Fried Chicken, popularly known as KFC, was born.

 

Remember, never give up, and always believe in yourself in spite of rejection.

title: Communication Breakdown
content:
This shows you how communication can get all muddied.

This is the letter the President wrote to the Academic Vice President, next Thursday Halley's Comet will appear over this area this is an event that occurs once every 75 years.  Call the division heads, have them assemble their professors and students on the athletic field, and explain this phenomenon to them.  If it rains, then cancel the observation and have classes to meet in the gym to see a film about a comet.

That was the President the Academic Vice President

Here is the Academic Vice President memo to the Division Chairman by order of the President next Thursday Halley's comet will appear over the athletic field, if it rains cancel classes or report to the gym with your professors and students where you will be shown films on this phenomenal event, which occurs only once every 75 years.

The Division Chairman to the professors by order the phenomenal President, next Thursday Halley's comet will appear in the gym.  In case of rain over the athletic field, the President will give another order something which occurs every 75 years.

Memo from the professor to the students, next Thursday the President will appear in our gym with Halley's comet, something which occurs every 75 years. If it rains, the President will cancel this comet and everything at our phenomenal athletic field.

Student writing home to parents. When it rains next Thursday over the athletic field the phenomenal 75-year-old president will cancel all classes and appear before the whole school in the gym accompanied by Bill Haley and the comets.

 

See what can happen when communication breaks down.

title: Congressman William Stanton(Ohio)
content:
Congressman William Stanton(Ohio) treasured a letter he received from the Chamber of Commerce dated 1949.  The letter read: “We feel that this year we really need a big-name speaker who’ll be a drawing card so we’re hoping to get the head football coach at John Carroll Univ.  Thanks anyhow for suggesting Representative John F. Kennedy.”   Who knows who the football coach was?  Herb Eisele

 

Do you have a potential JFK in your midst? Or a Bill Gates? Steve Jobs? Ray Kroc? Mother Teresa?  Mark Zuckerberg?

title: Consistency
content:
There is a reason it is hard to win back-to-back championships.  They can’t handle the perks of their first championship.  They start to show their trophy off, read the newspaper, and enjoy the perks of their success.  Then all of a succeed they begin to back off.

 

You see the perks that come with the first championship are the hindrances that come with the next one.  When a team wins their first championship, they don’t get the next one free.  That’s why this price thing is huge, the price is always going to be paid.  You must constantly pay the price.

 

2nd STORY:

Cal Ripken is in baseball HOF.  He wasn’t the best hitter.  He wasn’t the best fielder.  He wasn’t the best player, but he was the most consistent.  He played 2,632 consecutive games.  Wow, he showed up every day.  Not everyone shows up every day, but he did.

 

The Law of the Price Tag: The team fails to reach its potential when it fails to pay the price.

The Law of Consistency: Motivation gets you going–Discipline keeps you growing.

title: Control Your Temper (Anger)
content:
There once was a little boy who had a very bad temper. His father decided to hand him a bag of nails and said that every time the boy lost his temper, he had to hammer a nail into the fence.

On the first day, the boy hammered 37 nails into that fence.

 

The boy gradually began to control his temper over the next few weeks, and the number of nails he was hammering into the fence slowly decreased.  He discovered it was easier to control his temper than to hammer those nails into the fence.

 

Finally, the day came when the boy didn’t lose his temper at all. He told his father the news and the father suggested that the boy should now pull out a nail every day he kept his temper under control.

 

The days passed and the young boy was finally able to tell his father that all the nails were gone. The father took his son by the hand and led him to the fence.

 

“You have done well, my son, but look at the holes in the fence. The fence will never be the same. When you say things in anger, they leave a scar just like this one. You can put a knife in a man and draw it out. It won’t matter how many times you say I’m sorry, the wound is still there.”

 

Moral of the story:

Control your anger, and don’t say things to people in the heat of the moment, that you may later regret. Some things in life, you are unable to take back.

title: Customer Service
content:
Customer service is often so bad that we have come to expect and accept the worst.  Similar to this story about this person who saved for 15 years to buy a car.

He paid the dealer, then was told it would be 2 years before the car would be delivered.

 

The man didn’t get angry, he simply asked do you know what day 2 years from now?

The dealer wondered what difference it would make, but he still looked at his calendar and said exactly 2 years from today’s date.

 

The man looked worried, and then he asked do you know if it will be delivered in the morning or the afternoon?

 

Visibly irritated the dealer checked the schedule and said in the afternoon.

The man’s face lit up.  That’s great he said, because the plumbers coming in the morning. LOL

title: Desire
content:
A long while ago, a great warrior faced a situation which made it necessary for him to make a decision which ensured his success on the battlefield.  He was about to send his armies against a powerful foe whose men outnumbered his own.

 

He loaded his soldiers into boats, sailed to the enemy’s country, unloaded soldiers and equipment, and then gave the order to burn the ships that had carried them.

 

Addressing his men before the first battle, he said, “You see, the boats are going up in smoke.  That means that we cannot leave these shores alive unless we win.  We now have no choice — we win — or we perish!”  They won.

 

The Lesson:

  • Every person who wins in an undertaking must be willing to burn his ships and cut all sources of retreat; only by doing so can one be sure to maintain that state of mind known as "A burning desire to win.”

 

  • You have to put it all on the line.
    • Most people overestimate the risk and underestimate their potential.

 

  • Every person who reaches the age of understanding of the purpose of money (winning) wishes for it.
    • Wishes will not bring riches (winning).
    • Desiring riches(to win) with the state of mind that becomes an obsession, then planning definite ways and means to acquire riches(to obtain a win) and backing those plans with persistence, but does not recognize failure will bring riches (will win).

content:
