Excerpts from a Cat’s diary:

 

Day 983 of my captivity, my captures continued to taunt me with dangling little objects.

 

The only thing that keeps me going is my dream of escape.

title: Don’t Let Go Of The Wheel
content:
Imagine a farmer gets up every single day, and he puts his grain on the back of the tractor, and he puts the tractor in gear, and he drives out a mile into the pasture to feed the cows and they all come running. He dumps the feed and goes back to the barn.

 

If he gets up every single day for ten, fifteen, or twenty years and starts the tractor, puts the feed on, puts it in gear, and goes out to the same field, what will eventually happen? He’ll build ruts on the path to the cows. Eventually, he could just get up, throw the grain on the back, start the tractor, put it in gear, and let go of the wheel. That tractor will take him right out to that same spot he’s been going to for years.

 

Apply this story to your life and ask: Have you let go of the wheel?

Do you have ruts that keep you doing the same thing every day?

 

It doesn’t necessarily mean your entire life is in a rut, but do you unconsciously do the same things daily, expecting a different result?

 

Do you have habits that make every day the same while simultaneously hoping an outside factor will change it? Maybe you’re waiting for a shift in the economy, a person to intervene on your behalf, or fate to present you with the winning lottery ticket.  Have you become the thermometer instead of the thermostat?

 

I’m not judging. It happens to us all. Most people have let go of the wheel. But it doesn’t have to stay that way. So here’s what’s important about that farmer’s story:

 

To change that farmer’s direction, to change his destination, he doesn’t have to make a dramatic 180-degree turn. It’s not like a New Year’s resolution where you feel the need to change everything about yourself. You don’t have to wake up tomorrow morning and start an entirely new routine –yoga and then meditate and then practice gratitude for an hour.

 

Yes, all those things are worthwhile, but all you have to do tomorrow is put yourself in the position of that farmer and turn that wheel a quarter of an inch. Just a tiny shift.

 

If he got up tomorrow and turned that wheel a quarter of an inch, by the time he got out a mile in the field, he wouldn’t even be able to see his old feeding grounds because he would be so far away. Those ruts would be no more, because he’d  be carving a new path, a quarter inch at a time.

 

The Lesson:

It does not take a big shift.  It does not require major change in your daily habits.  Just consistent small steps daily is all that is required.

title: Don’t Let Your Frogs(Friends) Discourage You
content:
As a group of frogs was traveling through the woods, two of them fell into a deep pit. When the other frogs crowded around the pit and saw how deep it was, they told the two frogs that there was no hope left for them.

 

However, the two frogs decided to ignore what the others were saying and they proceeded to try and jump out of the pit. 

 

Despite their efforts, the group of frogs at the top of the pit were still saying that they should just give up. That they would never make it out.

 

Eventually, one of the frogs took heed to what the others were saying and he gave up, falling down to his death. The other frog continued to jump as hard as he could. Again, the crowd of frogs yelled at him to stop the pain and just die.

 

He jumped even harder and finally made it out. When he got out, the other frogs said, “Did you not hear us?”

 

The frog explained to them that he was deaf. He thought they were encouraging him the entire time.

 

Moral of the story:

People’s words can have a big effect on other’s lives. Think about what you say before it comes out of your mouth. It might just be the difference between life and death.

title: DONKEY STAY DOWN
content:
One day, a farmer’s donkey fell down into a well. The animal cried for hours as the farmer tried to figure out what to do. Finally, he decided the animal was old, and the well needed to be covered up anyway; it just wasn’t worth it to retrieve the donkey.

 

He invited all his neighbors to come over and help him. They all grabbed a shovel and began to shovel dirt into the well. At first, the donkey didn’t realize what was happening and cried horribly. Then, to everyone’s amazement, he quieted down. A few shovelloads later, the farmer finally looked down the well.

 

He was astonished at what he saw. With each shovel of dirt that hit his back, the donkey was doing something amazing.

 

He would shake it off and take a step up. As the farmer’s neighbors continued to shovel dirt on top of the animal, he would shake it off and take a step up. Pretty soon, everyone was amazed as the donkey stepped up over the edge of the well and happily trotted off!

 

 

REFLECTION:

Like the donkey...

1. Have you ever had dirt thrown on you? Yes or No? (Circle one)

 

2. What kind of dirt was it? Write your answer below.   ___________________________________________________

3. When there was a problem, did you act like the farmer and try to cover it up, or did you act like the donkey and rise above it?

_________________________________________________________________

 

HOW MY ATTITUDE AFFECTS ME

As problems arise, there is a time to cry, reflect, strategize, and a time to act.

 

What is one problem you are facing that you will handle with a positive attitude?

title: DREAMS ADD VALUE TO YOUR WORK
content:
There is a story of a reporter who talked to three construction workers pouring concrete at a building site.  “What are you doing?” he asked the first worker. “I’m earning a paycheck,” he grumbled.

 

The reporter asked the same question of a second laborer, who looked over his shoulder and said, “What’s it look like I’m doing? I’m pouring concrete.”

 

Then he noticed a third man, who was smiling and whistling as he worked.  “What are you doing?” he asked the third worker.  He stopped what he was doing and said excitedly, “I’m building a shelter for the homeless.”  He wiped his hands clean on a rag and then pointed, “Look, over there is where the kitchen will be.  And that over there is the women’s dormitory. This here . . .”

 

The Lesson:

Each man was doing the same job. But only the third was motivated by a larger vision. The work he did was fulfilling a dream, and it added value to all his efforts.

title: Every day as 3 little boys
content:
Every day as 3 little boys would walk along the same route home from school, they would reach this high wall and always wonder what is behind that wall.  One day one of them had the idea of throwing his hat over the wall to see what was behind the wall, so he threw it over.  Then said, well now I have to go get my hat.  Then his friends didn’t want to be outdone and they wanted to see first-hand themselves, so they threw their hats over.

  • The question is, would you throw your hat over the wall?
  • Do you want to go to new places, make new discoveries, and push your limits of growth?
  • Sometimes that requires bold commitment.
  • Today, I’m asking you to throw your hat over the wall.  Get outside your comfort zone.

 

Talent is a gift, GREATNESS is a choice….

title: Everybody, Somebody, Anybody, and Nobody
content:
This is a story about four people named Everybody, Somebody, Anybody, and Nobody. There was an important job to be done and Everybody was asked to do it. Everybody was sure Somebody would do it. Anybody could have done it, but Nobody did it. Somebody got angry about that because it was Everybody’s job. Everybody thought Anybody could do it but Nobody realized that Everybody wouldn’t do it. It ended up that Everybody blamed Somebody when Nobody did what Anybody could have done.

 

The story could be summarized in any number of ways. It certainly brings to life scenarios and phenomena that many people experience on a regular basis:

  • Lack of accountability
  • Lack of Ownership
  • Lack of Responsibility
  • Finger Pointing
  • Blame Assigning

 

All of these scenarios will not only have a significantly negative effect on an organization’s ability to operate effectively, but they will also have a severely detrimental effect on the Customer Experience.

title: Everyone Has a Story in Life
content:
A 24-year-old boy seeing out from the train’s window shouted…

 

“Dad, look the trees are going behind!”

 

Dad smiled and a young couple sitting nearby, looked at the 24-year-old’s childish behavior with pity, suddenly he again exclaimed…

 

“Dad, look the clouds are running with us!”

 

The couple couldn’t resist and said to the old man…

 

“Why don’t you take your son to a good doctor?” The old man smiled and said…“I did and we are just coming from the hospital, my son was blind from birth, he just got his eyes today.”

 

The Lesson:

Every single person on the planet has a story. Don’t judge people before you truly know them. The truth might surprise you.

title: Excuses / Alibis
content:
An inmate at Butte County Jail in California explained his absence from jail to sheriff’s deputies in this way:

 

I was playing pole vault and I got too close to the wall and I fell over the wall.  When I regained my senses, I ran around to try and find a way back in, but being unfamiliar with the area, I got lost.  The next thing I knew I was in Chico.

 

The Lesson:

People seldom realize how weak their excuses are until they hear some from others.

 

This is also a good idea to do the 55 Alibias exercise from Napoleon Hill's Think & Grow Rich

title: Father’s Love
content:
ON 7th of December 1988, AN EARTHQUAKE DEVASTATED THE NORTHWESTERN SECTION OF ARMENIA, KILLING AN ESTIMATED 25,000 PEOPLE.

 

Just after the earthquake, in a small town, a father rushed to his son’s school and found that the school had been flattened. There was nothing left to find.

 

But he had no thought of turning back. He used to tell his son, “No matter what happens, I will always be there for you when you require me.”

 

Though his prospects appeared hopeless, the father began feverishly removing rubble from where he believed his son’s classroom had been. Other parents only wailed hopelessly… ”My son!” or “My daughter!” Some even told him to go back home, there was little chance that any of the children could be alive. Yet, he replied: “I had a promise to my son that I would be there for him anytime he required me. I have to dig now.”

 

Courageously, he did it all alone; no one volunteered to help him. He just wants to confirm for himself: “Is my boy alive or is he dead?” Finding strength and endurance for his son, the faithful, loving father continued to dig…for 8 hours…12…24…36 hours.

Then in the 38th hour, as he heaved away a heavy piece of rubble, he heard voices. “Armand!” he screamed.

 

A child’s voice responded: “Dad! It’s me…Armand!” Then he said,  “I told them not to worry. If you were alive, you would save me, and once you saved me, they’d be saved. You kept your promise dad, You did it, Dad!”

 

A few moments later, the dad was helping his son Armand and 13 more frightened, thirsty, and hungry boys and girls climb out of the debris. Free at last! When the building fell, these children were spared in a tent-like pocket.

 

When the whole town praised Armand’s dad, his explanation was, “I promised my son, ‘No matter what happens, I will be there for you!”

title: Fathers for Good
content:
Son: Daddy I want to get married

Dad: First say sorry.

Son: For what?

Dad: Say sorry.

Son: But for what, what did I do?

Dad: You first say sorry

Son: But what’s my fault?

Dad: You first say sorry.

Son: But WHY?

Dad: You first say sorry

Son: Please, at least tell me a reason.

Dad: You first say sorry

Son: OK, I am sorry

Dad: Now you are prepared, your training is complete. When you learn to say sorry for no reason, you can marry.

 

A Father’s love is incomparable to any other kind of love.

title: Fear Story: The Barber
content:
This story is about a barber who is full of fear and negativity.  He was talking with one of his customers, and the customer said, I’m going to Italy tomorrow.  The barber said, oh, I used to live in Rome.  He asked, what air carrier are you flying on?  The customer told him, and he said oh boy, that’s the worst carrier.  They are always late, their safety record is not good, and the seats are not comfortable.

The barber asked, what hotel are you staying at?  The customer tells him, and he replies, oh boy, not that one.  I know the hotel, and the service is really terrible.  I just hope you get towels.  I just hope you get towels.

The barber asked what are you gonna do when you get there.  The customer replies we are gonna have a sales meeting, and we are gonna present this sales plan, and we are hoping it will do well.  The barber says, oh, you don’t know Italians; they talk, but they don’t buy.  They don’t buy.  The customer is getting low in the chair, and you can see the disappointment on his face.  Then he mumbled what word Pope.  The barber said did I hear you say Pope.  The customer replied yes.  The barber, asked what about the Pope.

He said that since I was over there, I was hoping to be able to see the Pope.  The barber, who you don’t understand, the Pope only sees important people.  You are not gonna get to see the Pope.

A month later, the guy was back in the barbershop. The barber asked how did it go?  The customer said it was the most amazing trip of my life.  The airline you talked about was awesome; they were on time, my luggage made it, and the landing was great.  In fact, the landing was so good that the flight attendant had to wake me up when we landed because I was asleep.  The hotel you told me about, when I walked in to register, they were all standing there waiting to hand me fresh towels.  It was awesome.  I could see the Vatican from my balcony.  The Italians loved it so much they have already placed orders, and I have to go back there.  This was the best sales meeting I ever had.

He said the highlight of my trip, I got to see the Pope.  The barber got so excited that he said, “You got to see the Pope; you have to tell me about it. I never knew anyone who saw the Pope.”

He said, well, they brought me into this long room.  I walked up the aisle with a red carpet and gilded gold everywhere, and as I got closer to the Pope, I felt more and more humble.   Once I got in front of him, I just fell to my knees and bowed.  He put his hand out, and I kissed his ring.  I scouted out your holiness, your holiness.  He put his hands on my head to bless me.  He looked and looked at both sides of my head and said, “My son, my son, where did you get such a lousy haircut?”

title: Feed Your Faith
content:
In the tail of two wolves, the grandfather was telling his grandson there are 2 wolves within you.  One bad and one good.

 

The grandson looked at his wise grandfather and asked, which one will live within me?  The grandfather says the one you feed.

 

The Lesson:

Think about it, you can either feed your faith or you can feed your fears. But if you feed your faith you will starve your fears and doubts.  On the same token, if you feed your fears, you will starve your faith.

title: Feeding The Hogs
content:
There was a cartoon in the New Yorker Magazine in which the farmer is feeding the hogs.  He filled entire trough up to the brim, and one pig suspiciously asked another in the group, have you ever wondered why he is so good to us?  LOL

Something beyond this…  What are our motives?

 

Used in influence discussions

title: Forrest Gump and St Peter
content:
Forrest Gump dies and goes to heaven. He's at the Pearlie Gates and met by St Peter himself. However, the gates are closed, and Forrest approaches the gatekeeper.  St Peter says, well, Forrest, it's certainly good to see you. We've heard a lot about you. I must tell you, though, that the place is filling up fast, and we've been administering an entrance examination for everyone.  The test is short, but you have to pass it before you can get into heaven.

 

Forrest responds, sure is good to be here, sir.  But nobody ever told me about any entrance exam, I sure hope the test ain't too hard.  Life was a big enough test as it was. St Peter goes on. Yes, I know, Forrest, but the test is only three questions.

 

  1. First, What two days of the week begin with the letter T?
  2. Second, how many seconds are there in a year?
  3. Third, what is God's first name?

 

Forrest leaves to think about the questions over.  He returns the next day and sees St Peter, who wakes him up and says…,

 

Now that you've had a chance to think the questions over tell me your answers.  Forrest says, “Well, the first one, which two days of the week began with the letter T, shucks, that one's easy. That'd be today and tomorrow. The Saints eyes open wide, and he exclaims, Forrest that's not what I was thinking, but you do have a point.  And I guess I didn't specify, so I'll give you credit for that answer.

 

How about the next one? ask St Peter.  How many seconds in a year?

 

Now that one's harder, says Forrest. But I thought and thought about that, and I guess the only answer can be 12.  Confounded, St Peter says, 12?  12?  Forrest, how in Heaven's name could you come up with 12 seconds in a year?  Forrest says there's got to be 12: “January 2,  February 2, March 2…”  “Hold it,” interrupts St. Peter.   I see where you're going with this, and I see your point…  though that wasn't quite what I had in mind… I'll give you credit for that one, too.

 

Let's go on with the third and final question. “Can you tell me God's first name”?

 

“Sure,” Forrest replied,  “It's Andy.”  Andy?  exclaimed an exasperated and frustrated St. Peter.  Okay, I can understand how you came up with your answers for my first two questions, but just how in the world did you come up with the name Andy as the first name of God?  “Shucks, that was the easiest one of all,” Forrest replied.

 

I learned it from the song, “Andy walks with me, Andy he talks with me, Andy he tells me I am his own.”  Saint Peter opened the Pearly Gates and said, “Run, Forrest, run.”

 

The Lesson:

Everyone Communicates, but Few Connect folks.  This is the perfect example of why connecting during communication is important.

title: Frogs on a log
content:
5 frogs are on a log and 4 decided to jump.

How many frogs are left on the log?

 

The Answer: 5 frogs are still on the log.

They decided to jump but didn’t take the action to jump.

How many times have you made a decision to do something, but didn’t follow through with action?

 

The Lesson:

Good intentions are worthless until you take action.

title: Frying Pan Story
content:
• A little boy was fishing, he caught 2 small fish that he had in his bucket.  Then suddenly he caught a BIG fish, he reeled it in, unhooked it, and threw the fish back.  When asked why did he that, the little boy replied my frying pan is only 9 inches wide.
  • This story makes me aware of how a person’s thinking can limit them.  So….

 

What is your frying pan story? (let them answer)

title: Funny Firsts
content:
As you deliver one of the openers below, think about how your body language can reinforce the message.

 

 

“If you are wondering if this will be a boring presentation, you are not alone. I’m dying to know too.”

 

“I’d like to make three important points. That’s the first one. Can’t remember the other two.”

 

“They said to keep it short and simple, so thanks for listening, and goodbye.”

 

“You’re thinking, how will I start? Don’t. Your real problem is when will I stop.”

 

“Some of you have heard me speak before. The rest of you have something to look forward to.”

 

“I’ve been working on this material for months. Fortunately, last night my dog ate it.”

title: Gandhi was such a transformational leader
content:
Gandhi was such a transformational leader.  When he left prison there were only 6 people with him, by the time he got to the sea there were 1 million.  It took him 54 years to see India become independent.  He was attached, rejected, imprisoned, misrepresented, sick, and finally victorious.  

 

Here’s what he said, “First they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight you and then you win.”  Isn’t that true?

title: God created it all (funny story)
content:
On the 1st day, God created a dog.

God said all day sit at the door at your house and bark at anybody that comes by and I’m gonna give you a 20 year life span.

The dog said that’s too long.  Give me 10 years and I will give you back 10 years.  God agreed.

 

On the 2nd day, God created a monkey.

God said entertain people, do monkey tricks and I’m gonna give you a 20 year life span.

The monkey said how boring, he said the dog gave back 10 years, I’m gonna do the same also.  God agreed.

 

On the 3rd day, God created a cow.

God said go out in the field all day long, have fun under the sun, have calves and I’m gonna give you a life span of 60 years.

The cow said that is kind of a tough life you want me to live for 60 years.

He said let me have 20 years and I will give you back the other 40 years.  God agreed.

 

On the 4th day, God created man.

God said you go out eat, sleep, play, marry, have children and I’m gonna give you 20 years of life.

The man said, what only 20 years?

He said I tell you what, I will take my 20 years, plus the 40 years the cow gave back, pause the 10 years the monkey gave back, plus the 10 years the dog gave back.  That makes 80 years.  God agreed.

 

The Lesson:

  • So that’s why the 1st 20 years of our lives we eat, we sleep, we play, marry and enjoy ourselves.
  • For the next 40 years we slave in the sun working all day to support our family.
  • For the next 10 years we do monkey tricks to entertain our grandchildren.
  • Then for the last 10 years we sit on the front porch bark at everybody and everything.

title: Growth happens below the surface
content:
I don’t have to see evidence....

 

A group of 6th Graders had a project to grow a plant.

 

Each student received a cup, a pile of dirt, one seed, and a cup of water.

 

Day 1

They filled the cup with dirt, and put our seed in the dirt, then they watered the seed.

 

Day 2

They ran into the classroom to see if they saw any growth, but each student said, “It’s not working.” Because they didn’t see anything.

 

Day 3

They ran into the classroom to see if they saw any growth, but each student said, “It’s not working.” Because they didn’t see anything.

 

Day 4

They walked into the classroom to see if they saw any growth, but each student said, “It’s not working.” Because they didn’t see anything.

 

Day 5

None of the students checked their cup to see if it was working.  One girl decided to go to her cup to check.  When she got to the cup, she looked in it and shouted out, “It’s working.”  So, all the kids ran to their cups to see if it was working.

 

You see what those kids didn’t realize, just like the Law of Process: Leaders develop daily, not in a day. They didn’t realize that those seeds were developing below the surface even though they did not see any evidence of it.  That is the same thing with you as you go through this training, you are developing and getting better daily, so just because you don’t see overnight success doesn’t mean you are not progressing.  That doesn’t mean it not happening below the surface.

 

WRITE DOWN:

I don’t have to see the evidence to know it’s working.

 

Growth/Leadership Development:

Personal growth is like the Chinese bamboo sticks. Chinese bamboo stick takes 5 years to pop above the surface then once it pops up you can visually see it growing.  But You have to water and fertilize for all that time. In fact, in 5 weeks once it is above the surface, it can grow up to 90 feet tall.  Personal growth works similarly, it works behind the scenes, YOU MAY NOT SEE EVIDENCE OF IT for a while because it is growing inside of you.  But you have to keep fertilizing and watering, and then one day all of a sudden it will show unbelievable growth.  However, your friends and your colleagues may ridicule you, they may laugh it and tease that nothing has changed.  You see some of them quit on their dream, and some of them gave up on their goals, but if you keep going, you will be like that bamboo tree.  You will shoot up in the sky:

  1. Your scores get better
  2. Your overall performance improves
  3. You start to think differently
  4. You start to walk differently
  5. Your mindset changes
  6. Your bank account changes
  7. Your friends change

 

You see everything about you, your team, and your students, become bigger, better, and Significant.  And once you have tasted significance, success will never be satisfied.  Success is adding value to yourself; significance is adding value to someone else.

 

SAY IT:

I don’t have to see the evidence to know it’s working.

title: Happiness
content:
A professor gave a balloon to every student, who had to inflate it, write their name on it, and throw it in the hallway. The professor then mixed all the balloons. The students were then given 5 minutes to find their own balloon. Despite a hectic search, no one found their balloon.

 

At that point, the professor told the students to take the first balloon that they found and hand it to the person whose name was written on it. Within 5 minutes, everyone had their own balloon.

 

The professor said to the students: "These balloons are like happiness. We will never find it if everyone is looking for their own. But if we care about other people's happiness, we'll find ours too."

title: Help is Just a Call Away
content:
A man slaughtered a big cow, lit the grill, and said to his daughter.

 

“Daughter, call our friends and neighbors to eat with us... let us feast!"

 

His daughter took to the street and started shouting.

 

“Please help us put out a fire at my Dad's house!".

 

After a few moments, a small group of people came out, and the rest acted like they didn't hear the cry for help.

 

Those who came ate and drank until late.

 

The stunned father turned to his daughter and said to her.

 

“The people who came, I didn’t know them and had never seen them before, so where are our friends and neighbors?"

 

The daughter said.

 

“Those who came out of their homes came to help us put out a fire in our house and not for the party.  These are the ones who deserve our generosity and hospitality.”

 

Conclusion:

It will not always be those closest to you that will volunteer to help you. Sometimes, you have to leave home to enjoy your greatest success.

 

But remember this when you hear your friends asking for your help in business.

title: Hot Air Balloon - Management
content:
This man in a hot air balloon was traveling but realized he was lost, so he descended close to the ground.  He spotted a lady below and yelled out, “Excuse me can you help me, I promised a friend I would meet them, but I don’t know where I am.”

 

The woman replied, “You are in a hot air balloon, hovering approximately 30 ft above the ground and gave him his longitude and latitude position.  You must be an engineer said the balloonist.  I am replied the lady.  How did you know?  He said well, all the info you gave me is technically correct but I have no idea what to make of your information and the fact is I’m still lost.

 

Frankly, you have not been much help at all, in fact, you have helped delay my trip.

 

The woman below responded you must be in management.  I am, replied the balloonist.  How did you know?

 

Well, said the woman,  you don’t know where you are or where you are going. You have risen to where you are due to a large quantity of hot air.  You made a promise that you have no idea how to keep and expect people beneath you to solve your problem.  The fact is, you are in the same position you were in before we met and somehow it is my fault.

title: Imagine your swim team has just won the state meet
content:
Imagine your swim team has just won the state meet.  You and your teammates are so overjoyed that you pick up your swim coach and haul him over to the pool, where you plan to throw him into the water for a celebration dunking.  All of a sudden, the coach starts screaming, “No! No! Put me down.  I can’t swim.

 

How surprised would you be?

 

Your coach implied he was a great swimmer.  Even though you won the meet, how much trust will you have for your coach now that you have found out he misled you?

 

The Lesson:

Too many times we are so concerned about the end result that we try to take a shortcut to get there.  THERE ARE NO SHORTCUTS WHEN INTEGRITY IS INVOLVED.  Eventually, the truth will come out.

 

Integrity Matters

title: John Wooden: Make Every Day Your Masterpiece
content:
He noticed a player that wasn’t giving 100%, so he asked the player what was wrong.

He responded I’m feeling tired because of school work, his girlfriend, and other issues.

 

So Coach asked him, what percentage of effort would you say you are giving me today?

The player said, “I believe I’m giving 80% effort today.”

 

Coach Wooden said, so let me tell you something.  I know you may be thinking today I’m only giving 80% but tomorrow I will make up for it and give 120%.

 

He said, I just want you to know that is impossible.  You can’t give more than 100%, so if you are only giving 80% today, that 20% is lost forever.

title: Jorge Rodriquez – The Bank Robber
content:
Jorge Rodriguez was an Old West bank robber from Mexico who operated along the Texas border around 1900. Rodriguez was so successful that the Texas Rangers established a special force to try and stop him.

 

Late one afternoon, one of these special rangers saw Rodriguez slipping across the border back into Mexico and trailed him at a discreet distance. He watched as the outlaw returned to his home village and mingled with the people in the square. When Rodriquez went into his favorite cantina to relax, the Ranger slipped in and managed to get the drop on him.

 

With a pistol to the bank robber’s head, the law man said, “Jorge Rodriguez, I know who you are. I’ve come to get back all the money that you have stolen from the banks in Texas. Unless you give it to me, I am going to blow your brains out.”

 

Rodriguez could see the man’s badge, and he could discern his hostile intent. But there was a problem. He didn’t speak English. He began speaking rapidly in Spanish. But the ranger couldn’t understand what he said, because he didn’t speak Spanish.

 

Just then a young boy came up and said in English, “I can help. I speak English and Spanish. Do you want me to be your translator?”

The ranger nodded. The boy quickly explained everything the ranger had said.

 

Nervously, Rodriguez answered, “Tell the big Texas ranger that I have not spent a cent of the money. If he will go to the town well, face north, count down five stones, he will find a loose one there. Pull it out and all the money is behind there. Please tell him quickly.”

 

The boy looked back at the ranger and said, “Senor, Jorge Rodriguez is a brave man. He says he is ready to die.”

 

The Lesson:

#1 The ability to connect with others begins with Understanding the Value of People.

 

#2 Why do I not need to interpret this story for most of you, because when the truth does not serve your purposes, all of a sudden truth does not matter.

title: Keep the big picture in perspective
content:
Story: Before we get started, let me share one of the funniest stories I have come across in terms of connecting requires energy(effort).  This is the story of a college student who is in a little trouble, so she is writing to her mother at home.

 

“Dr Mom, since I’ve been away at college one full semester, I think it is time for me to bring you up to date as to what is going on. Shortly after I arrived at college, I got bored with dormitory life, and I stole $10 out of my roommate’s purse. With the money, I rented a Honda bike and crashed it into a telephone pole a few blocks away from my dorm room.  I also broke my leg, but no worries, I was rescued by a young doctor who lives upstairs in the apartment house on the corner.  He took me in, nursed me back to good health, set my leg, and thanks to him I’m moving around again.

 

Wanted to let you know we are going to be married as soon as possible since we are having some trouble with the blood test because there is a disease that keeps showing up.  We do hope, however we will be married before the baby arrives, and we will be home shortly thereafter to live with you and Dad.  I know you will love the baby as much as you have loved me, even though it will be of a different religion.  Please try to understand that the reason we have to come home and live with you and Dad is that my doctor friend wants out of medical school because of all the attention he was giving to me because of my condition.

 

Really, Mom, I didn’t steal $10 from my roommate’s purse, rent a Honda bike, hit a telephone pole, or break my leg.  I did not meet a young doctor of a different religion nor are we going to be married.  There is no disease, test, or baby to worry about.  And I won’t be at home to live with you and Dad, nor will he either.  Mom, it took a lot of energy to write this letter. I am getting a D in Chemistry, and I’m getting an F in Economics, and I wanted you to accept these grades in their proper perspective.

title: Kentucky Derby Story
content:
There was a man that tried to enter his mule into the Kentucky Derby, he was immediately rebuked and disqualified. Your mule has no chance of winning against some of the top thoroughbreds, the race organizers told him.

I know, the man replied, but I thought the associations would do him some good.

 

The Lesson:

  • Being around people who are better than we are has a tendency to make us stretch ourselves.
  • Yes, it may not always be comfortable, but it is always profitable.

 

Great people will try to bring out the greatness in others. Small people will try to put the same limitations on you as they put on themselves.

title: Kobe Bryant Mindset
content:
When Kobe was asked by an Alabama football player, “Is he more motivated by the will to win or just by hating to lose?” He responded, “by neither”. He replied, “I’m motivated by being the best player I can be.”

 

So I ask, “Are you motivated to be the best leader you can be?”

title: Koi Fish Size
content:
A man recently told a story of the Japanese Koi and how it lacked perspective and limited its growth based on its surroundings.

 

• When in a bowl, it grows to 2 inches…

 

• When in a tank, it grows to 8 inches…

 

• When in a pond, it grows to 18 inches…

 

• When in a lake, it grows to 42 inches…

 

The Koi fish always has the potential to be 42 inches, but its environment can restrict it, and so can we. God desires us to always grow to our potential, but our thinking and our environment can confine us; it can constrict us.

 

The Lesson:

We must learn how to defy the box other people try to put us in and live up to the possibilities God has designed for us.  Some people have already created a box for you as they were creating a limited box for themselves; they want you to stay small, too.

You will never become what you are supposed to become until you defy the box others are trying to put you in. In other words, you have to give up to go up. Give up:

  • Bad habits and create good ones
  • Negative thoughts and generate positive thoughts
  • Limited thinking people and develop relationships with growth mindset individuals
  • Destructive behaviors and create uplifting behaviors

 

IT IS TIME TO BREAK OUT!

title: Leadership Culture - Solid core values build a strong foundation
content:
Business Wins by Realigning to its Roots — Thanks to Vision of Rick Keyes

 

“Our culture is the secret sauce at Meijer,” declared Rick. “It’s what we live and breathe on. But coming out of the recession prior to me coming into the role as CEO, we had started to drift a bit on the culture within our organization.”

A fresh perspective for a family business: Get back to what makes you strongest

When Rick was offered the chance to lead Meijer, the first-ever non-Meijer family member to take on the CEO role, he was very clear up front that he intended to take profits down even further in order to realign the company back to its core values. Meijer boldly supported him in this decision. “We took our entire strategy, we set it aside and we said we're going to build a strategic focus that every single person in the company can understand.

It can be boiled down to three concepts:

  1. We’re putting the customer at the center of our decisions.
  2. We're going to win with our team, and we’re going to be relentless about making sure that we enable and empower our teams to win.
  3. We're going to have a passion to compete.

“All of a sudden you could see our team just light up with engagement,” said Rick. “

These improvements include a company that's now 70,000 team members strong with approximately 19 billion dollars in revenue.

 

Take Away

The Law of Buy-In: People buy into the leader then the vision.

title: A little girl and a big stick of cotton candy
content:
ony Campolo (Author) tells the story of a little girl who had this big stick of cotton candy.  This young man saw it and said wow that is a huge stick of cotton candy, he asked how can you eat all of that?  The little girl said well it’s very easy sir, I’m a lot bigger on the inside than I am on the outside.

I want to tell you, that character is bigger on the inside than on the outside.  It’s an inside job.

Character is not made in crisis it is revealed in crisis.

title: LOBSTER
content:
• James is a guy that loves to go fishing.  He goes as much as possible.
  • He went out to fish for lobsters one day and took a haul of 125 lobsters.
  • He came home, prepped them, and put them in his freezer.  He said I have enough lobster for an entire year.
  • He was so excited about it that one of his friends came over and he told him about the big lobster catch.
  • He asked him, would you like a couple?  The friend said yes, of course.
  • That felt so good, he asked. I wonder who else would like some lobsters?
  • So, he started calling his friends and he said that for the next 3 days, he had like a lobster trail to his house.
  • He felt so good and said that after about 4 days, he looked in the freezer, and he only had 3 lobsters left.
  • Then he thought, wow, that was kind of stupid.  I had enough lobsters for a year, and now I only have 3 left.
  • He said, I went away for a few days and came back.  I walked into my garage, and there was this terrible smell.   He wondered, what was that?
  • He tracked the smell back to his freezer and realized the power had gone out on the freezer.
  • He opened the door and looked; sure enough those 3 lobsters had gone bad.
  • He thought, OMG.  Then after a while he started to feel good.
  • He thought, I’m sure glad I gave those other lobsters away.
  • I added value to someone else, otherwise they could have all been lost.
  • He said, it totally changed the way I think.  He felt, the only lobsters I saved where the lobsters I gave away.

 

The Lesson:

  • The only lobsters of value where the ones I gave to other people.  So the point is,  just add as much value to others as much as possible.

title: Mahatma Gandhi: What I Think is What I Feel
content:
Mahatma Gandhi spoke to parliament for 2 hours without notes. Afterward, a reporter asked Gandhi’s assistant how could he speak for so long without notes.  The Assistant replied,

 

“You don’t understand Gandhi, “You see, what he thinks is what he feels.  What he feels is what he says.  What he says is what he does.  What Gandhi feels, what he thinks, what he says, and what he does are all the same.  He does not need notes.”

 

The Lesson:

When values, thoughts, feelings, and actions are all in alignment, a person becomes focused and his character is strengthened.  That allows a leader to lead himself successfully.

 

Have participants repeat after me:

What I think is what I feel

What I feel is what I say

What I say is what I do

title: Man treated wife bad
content:
There was this couple that had been married for 30+ years. The wife was nice, meek, and mild. She did everything to support her husband. She was a well-educated woman.

 

The husband on the other hand was mean and never treated his wife well. He never complimented her, he never appreciated anything she did. He wasn’t a well-educated man, but she still loved him.

 

One day the wife died and her spirit went to heaven. As she arrived at the pearly gates, St Peter was waiting there for her. He said, “In order to cross the line, you must spell this word correctly.”  She said ok, what is the word. He replied, “Faithful”.

She spelled it correctly so he let her in. And said, welcome in.

 

Then all of a sudden 2 other people died. St Peter said I have to go handle a burning issue on the other side, I’ll be back.  You handle anyone who comes here. She said, well how do I know if they are allowed in? He replied, just like I did you, ask them to spell a word. She asked, what word? He said any word. Then he left.

 

Then she heard footsteps, she looked and it was her husband. He looked at her and said oh lord, baby we made it. We both made it to heaven. He said, baby, I’m so sorry for the way I treated you, I really never meant it. I’m truly sorry.

 

She said, well you haven’t made it yet. He said what do you mean? She said, you still have to spell a word to cross this line. He asked, what word?  She paused and looked at him, then said, “ambidextrous.”

 

The Lesson:

Watch out how you treat people today because they may be able to impact you tomorrow.  Focus on adding value to others.

title: Many years ago there was a great tragedy
content:
Many years ago there was a great tragedy after about 6 people who died trying to climb Mount Everest.  Mike Wallace of  CBS (60 Minutes) was interviewing one of the tour guides:

 

Mike Wallace: If you wouldn’t have had tourists with you, could have gotten to the top by yourself.

Tour guide: Yes, without a doubt, we would have been able to get to the top without them, and/or we would have been able to save our own lives. But then he looked at Mike Wallace and said, but that’s not the job of a tour guide.  The job of a tour guide is to take people places they would never be able to go on their own. Our job is not to go to the top alone, it is to take somebody with us. We sometimes die in our duty.

 

Mike Wallace: But you risk your life, why do you risk your life?

Tour guide: Mr. Wallace, it’s obvious to me that you have never been to the top of a mountain.

 

That’s what we do as a leader, take people to places they could never experience on their own. When you are a great leader, the people around you will go to places they would never go on their own. And there is great joy and fulfillment in that fact.

title: Military Stories
content:
This happened to a friend of mine during the German Commando course:

The last week of this training is an exercise with very long marches where you carry a heavy backpack.

Before the exercise started, the instructors checked the soldiers’ backpacks to make sure that none of them tried to cheat by “forgetting” some of the heavier items.

 

My friend got busted. He had forgotten to pack three items! As a punishment, his instructor gave him a big and heavy 10 kilo (20 pounds) rock and told him:

 

”You will carry this rock for the whole week, and at the end of the exercise, you will give it back to me!”

 

My friend’s group started the march, and when they turned around the first corner and were out of the instructor’s sight, he dumped the rock.

 

Unfortunately, the instructor hadn’t forgotten the whole story, and at the end of the exercise, he approached my friend and asked for his rock. My friend said:

 

“Dear Mr. Oberleutnant, I am sorry, but I lost your rock. Of course, as soon as I realized I lost it, I looked for a replacement rock. Unfortunately, however, the best one I could find was this one:”

 

My friend reached with one hand in his trouser pocket, and out of it he produced a tiny stone, not bigger than a walnut. He gave the stone to his instructor.

The instructor became very serious and held the stone in front of his eyes to see it better. Then he took a pencil out of his breast pocket, gave a pencil and stone to my friend, and said:

“Something like this has never happened to me before! Sign the stone, I want to keep it as a souvenir!”

They both started laughing.

title: Monkeys Pulling each other down
content:
We have all been pulled down by others. (ASK: Have you ever been pulled down by someone?)

 

Let me tell you about an experiment that researchers did with 4 monkeys.

 

They brought these 4 monkeys in a closed room, and they had a tree for them to climb to the top of where they had a big bucket of bananas.  Automatically when the monkeys came into the room, the first monkey started to go up the tree, when that monkey got right up to where the bananas were, they doused him with a bunch of cold water.  The monkey ran back down the tree.

 

Then the 2nd monkey saw the bananas and ran up the tree and when he got close to the bananas, they doused him with a bunch of cold water.  He ran right back down the tree.

 

You can see what happened, the next few monkeys tried to climb, each monkey was doused, and each of them came back down.

 

And then they took one monkey out of the room and replaced him with a monkey that had not gone through that bad experience(cold drenching water). And automatically that new monkey tried to climb the tree, but the other 3 monkeys that had the bad experience pulled him down.  They would not let him climb.  There was no need for water now because the other monkeys were pulling him down.

 

Slowly, the researchers pulled one monkey out of the room until there was no monkey in the room that had experienced the water drenching.  So now, there were 4 monkeys in the room who had never been doused with water, but they kept pulling each other down so that they wouldn’t reach the bananas, but they didn’t know why.  But they pull each other down anyway.

 

Each one of us has been pulled down by people who have not necessarily experienced something bad in an area, but they have heard someone has experienced something bad in an area, so they pull us down.

title: Montgomery Wards
content:
A salesman who envisioned selling goods directly from manufacturers to rural customers founded Montgomery Ward in 1872. The company was well established by 1900. It even came to own the biggest skyscraper west of Manhattan. But, over the years, Wards failed to keep pace with changing times and new methods. By 2000, it was out of business. Afraid to pay the price of keeping up, Wards lost everything. Teams must pay a price to win.

 

*It wasn’t a resource issue, it was a willingness to pay the price(spend).

 

The Law of the Price Tag: The team fails to reach its potential when it fails to pay the price.

title: Mount Everest
content:
A guide who took a team to climb to the top of Mount Everest fell into a major storm, so they had to turn around.  Obviously, they were all upset because of the major expense, a lot of time and effort.  The guide knew they were all disappointed, so he said we all will have dinner at the lounge before we go home tomorrow.  They had dinner, there was a somber mood.  As they wrapped up this low-key dinner, the guide stood up to speak.  Right behind him was a big picture of Mount Everest on the wall, in fact, the picture was about the size of the wall.  Then he turned his back to the people who didn’t make it to the top and started talking to the picture.

 

Here is what he said, “Mount Everest, I want to say something to you tonight. We tried to conquer you today, but we failed, you defeated us.  But Mount Everest I want to say something else to you, we are coming back next year.  I want you to know that you defeated us today, but we will defeat you next year.  Let me tell you why, Mount Everest, you are as big as you will ever get.  But the people on this team, WE CAN GET BIGGER. WE CAN BECOME BETTER, WISER, STRONGER, FASTER.

 

That’s the law of Mount Everest, gather your team, grow your team, and go all the way to the top.  As the challenge escalates, the need for teamwork elevates.

title: MY GROWTH JOURNEY
content:
My growth journey from here to there has often been lonely, the reason is I’m willing to admit wrong because of my desire to grow and change.

Growth is a result of bad habits dropped, wrong priorities changed and new ways of thinking embraced.  Many are not willing to admit wrong so that they can discover right, therefore they cling to right and their life turns out wrong.  How sad, surrender of being right is a prerequisite to finding right.

title: Never judge others by their NO.
content:
Once a bird was searching for a home to lay her eggs and get shelter in the coming rainy season.

 

In her search, she saw two trees and went to ask for shelter.

 

When she asked about the first tree. He refused to give her shelter.

 

With disappointment, she went to the second.

 

And second, agreed

 

She made her home and laid her eggs and then the rainy season arrived.

The rain was so heavy that the first tree fell and was carried away by the flood.

 

The bird saw this and in a taunting way said: ” See, this is your karma, you didn’t offer me shelter, now God has given you the punishment.”

 

The tree smiled and said: ” I knew I was not going to survive this rainy season that’s why I refused you. I didn’t want to risk your and your children’s lives.“

 

The bird had tears in her eyes. Now she knew the reason and felt respect for the tree.

 

Moral of the Story:

We should not always consider someone’s NO as their arrogance. You don’t know the full picture. Respect other’s decisions whether it is in your favor or not.

 

We get so much involved in the problems that we forget to view the other person’s point. Without even trying to understand the motive, the reason, we make our own judgments. We should never judge others by their No. because we don’t know their story.

 

You don’t know what good is hidden for you behind it.

title: Nursing Students - Cleaning Lady’s Name
content:
I love the story of these nursing students who were taking their final exam, the last question on the test was “What is the name of the cleaning lady that cleans our room?”  Some of the students raised their hands and said, I don’t understand the question.  Is this a real question on the test and is it going to count?

The professor said of course it is gonna count just as much as all the other questions.  He said, you have to understand you are not in the medical business, you are in the people business.

And knowing the name of the cleaning lady is going to be essential for everything else you do in life.  What was he saying, “You need to value everyone”.

title: NY Police Chief - Law of Intentionality
content:
Law of Intentionality - Growth doesn’t happen automatically.

 

When NY Police Chief William Bradley took office:

  • There was a lot of crime in New York City(NYC)
  • He brought in his 6 leaders and asked them if they believed they could drastically cut crime in NYC.
    • 4 said NO, they didn’t believe they could. They felt they could hold it steady, but not drastically cut it.
    • 2 said YES,
  • For the 2 that said YES, he shook their hand and said you are going to help me with this transformation.
  • For the 4 that said NO they didn’t believe they could drastically cut crime, he FIRED them.
  • He said I can’t have anyone on my police team that doesn’t believe we can make a positive difference.

 

  • Transformation starts with your belief that you can make a difference.
    • By valuing people
    • By being honest & having integrity with people.
    • By being intentional
    • By providing a great service to your team.

title: Old Man and Frogs

The old man picked up the frog and put it into his pocket.

The frog then said, I told you to pick me up, kiss me and I will turn into a beautiful bride.

title: On God’s Time
content:
A man walked to the top of a hill to talk to God.

The man asked, “God, what’s a million years to you?” and God said, “A minute.”

Then the man asked, “Well, what’s a million dollars to you?” and God said, “A penny.”

Then the man asked, “God…..can I have a penny?” and God said, “Sure…..in a minute.”

title: One Liners
content:
1. To win, you must take control early; it’s like the first day you get married when your wife takes control early.
  2. Our communication was like the kid on 2nd chair French Horn in the school band; we had to play better.
  3. It’s a double-edged sword.  It’s like watching your mother-in-law drive off a cliff in a Cadillac.  You have mixed feelings.
  4. It’s kind of like a woodpecker in a petrified forest. Just keep busy and look for opportunities.
  5. I have a short memory, just like in 3rd grade.  Two of the best years of my life.
  6. One aspect, we looked like we were ready to play.  Another factor is that we look like we just got off Willie Nelson’s tour bus.
  7. His attitude is positive.  He thinks he can take on hell with a squirt gun.
  8. It’s sort of like a T-bone steak dinner with all the trimmings.  They played a complete game.
  9. Jacksonville (substitute any city) is so bad that they sentence prisoners to attend the game.
  10. Everybody expects you to win.  My wife couldn’t go to church with me one Sunday.  They were asking where she was.  I said she doesn’t go out with losers.
  11. I was so bad in school.  I remember one time I got an “A” in school, and my mom beat me for cheating.
  12. In God, we trust; all others pay cash.
  13. Like my grandfather said in business, “buy for a dime, sell for a dollar, and you don’t even have to keep books.”

title: Park My Car
content:
A lady walks into a bank in New York City before going on vacation and asks for a $5,000 loan.

The banker asks, “Okay, miss, is there anything you would like to use as collateral?”

The woman says, “Yes, of course. I'll use my Rolls Royce.”

The banker, stunned, asks, “A $250,000 Rolls Royce? Really?”

The woman is completely positive. She hands over the keys, as the bankers and loan officers laugh at her.

They check her credentials and make sure she is the title owner.

Everything checks out. They park it in their underground garage for two weeks.

When she comes back, she pays off the $5,000 loan as well as the $15.41 interest.

The loan officer says, "Miss, we are very appreciative of your business with us, but I have one question.

We looked you up and found out that you are a multi-millionaire. Why would you want to borrow $5,000?"

The woman replies, "Where else in New York City can I park my car for two weeks for only $15.41 and expect it to be there when I return?"

title: Pat Summit
content:
One of the greatest college basketball coaches of all time.

6 National Championships

 

At half time:

Players entered the dressing room, and coaches went to another room to talk.

One of the team captions would write on the board:

  • What they did right in 1st half
  • What they did wrong in 1st half
  • What they needed to change for 2nd half

 

Then, the coaches would come in and talk about 2nd half strategy.

 

She said that when she was a young coach, she was not good at it because she didn’t connect with her team.

She said she ASSUMED her players knew what she knew.

She said she ASSUMED when she was coaching, they were on the same page.

She felt she was “leading by assumption.”

She realized she had to find a way to find out where they were. So, she used the marker board to see what her players were thinking.

  • She could see if they knew what they did right.
  • She could see if they knew what they did wrong.

 

In just a few seconds, she could tell if her players understood the context of the game.

Once she found out where they were, she would coach them from that point.

She said that as a leader, you must find out where your people are before you can lead them.

 

Sometimes, a manager may say, “It’s lonely at the top.”

But that is not a leadership expression.

Leaders don’t look at themselves as “they are up here” and “their people are down there.”

If you are at the top alone, you are not a leader but a hiker.

 

My suggestion for you is to get OFF THE TOP OF THE HILL, then you won’t be lonely.

Go down to where the people are, walk slowly through the crowd, and help bring your people to the top with you.

 

Leadership by assumption will always cause us to have a disconnect.

Coach Summit helped us see that you have to find out where your team is before you can lead them.

As a leader, you must always ask yourself what you must do and what you must say to connect with your people.

title: Planting Trees & The Farmer
content:
This farmer on the porch noticed a highway department truck pull up on the road shoulder, and a man got out, dug a sizable hole in the ditch, and then got back in the vehicle.   

 

A few minutes later, the other truck occupant got out, filled the hole with dirt, and got back in the truck.

 

Then they drove forward on the shoulder about 50 yards and repeated the process. They were digging, waiting, refilling. After half a dozen repetitions, the farmer approached them and asked, “What are you doing? I’ve been watching you.” What are you doing?  Sir,  we're on a highway beautification project, the driver said, and the guy who plants the trees is homesick today.

 

Pause,

Obviously, they never understood the big picture, did they?  They never asked why we are doing what we’re doing and whether it has a natural effect on others.

title: Potatoes, Eggs, and Coffee Beans
content:
Once upon a time, a daughter complained to her father that her life was miserable and that she didn’t know how she would make it. She was tired of fighting and struggling all the time. It seemed that just as one problem was solved, another soon followed.

Her father, a chef, took her to the kitchen. He filled three pots with water and placed each on a high fire. Once the three pots began to boil, he put potatoes in one pot, eggs in the second pot, and ground coffee beans in the third pot.

He then let them sit and boil without saying a word to his daughter. The daughter moaned and impatiently waited, wondering what he was doing.

After twenty minutes, he turned off the burners. He took the potatoes from the pot and placed them in a bowl. He pulled the eggs out and put them in a bowl.  He then ladled the coffee out and placed it in a cup.

Turning to her, he asked. “Daughter, what do you see?”

“Potatoes, eggs, and coffee,” she hastily replied.

“Look closer,” he said, “and touch the potatoes.” She did and noted that they were soft. He then asked her to take an egg and break it. After pulling off the shell, she observed the hard-boiled egg. Finally, he asked her to sip the coffee. Its rich aroma brought a smile to her face.

“Father, what does this mean?” she asked.

He then explained that the potatoes, the eggs, and the coffee beans had each faced the same adversity– the boiling water.

However, each one reacted differently.

The potato went in strong, hard, and unrelenting, but it became soft and weak in boiling water.

The egg was fragile, with the thin outer shell protecting its liquid interior until it was put in the boiling water. Then, the inside of the egg became hard.

However, the ground coffee beans were unique. After they were exposed to the boiling water, they changed the water and created something new.

“Which are you,” he asked his daughter. “When adversity knocks on your door, how do you respond? Are you a potato, an egg, or a coffee bean? “

 

Moral: 

In life, things happen around us, things happen to us, but the only thing that truly matters is what happens within us.


Which one are you?

title: President Theodore Roosevelt
content:
President Theodore Roosevelt was a man of action, but he was also a good listener, and he appreciated that in other people.  Once at a gala ball, he grew tired of meeting people who returned his remarks with stiff, mindless pleasantries.  So, he began greeting people with a smile, saying “I murdered my grandmother this morning.”  Most people were so nervous about meeting him that they did not respond.  One diplomat whispered to him, “I’m sure she had it coming to her!”.

 

THE POINT: The only way to find out what you’re missing is to start listening.

title: Pro golfer Richard Lee
content:
Pro golfer Richard Lee said when he was early in his career and had a bad shot, he used to get really down on himself and he would get really disappointed.  And his negative emotions would start to fill his mind and hurt his play for the rest of the tournament.

 

One day his mother-in-law said to him, “You will always have days when you make bad shots.”  Every golfer does.  As you walk toward your ball you have a decision to make:  Will I dread seeing the lie of the ball and begin filling your mind with negative thoughts and my body with negative emotions?

 

Or will you welcome the ball and be glad you are a golfer and realize that you have an opportunity to make a great recovery shot?

 

If you always welcome the ball regardless of your lie, you will more often make good recovery shots.

 

Richard now says, “Wherever his ball lies, he walks up to it and welcomes the ball.  It has made a great difference in his game.

 

What a great way to think of dealing with adversity: make a recovery shot!

 

 

From No Limits Mastermind

title: Puppies for Sale
content:
A shop owner placed a sign above his door: “Puppies For Sale.”


Signs like this always have a way of attracting young children, and to no surprise, a boy saw the sign and approached the owner; 

 

“How much will you sell the puppies for?” he asked.

 

The store owner replied, “Anywhere from $30 to $50.”

The little boy pulled out some change from his pocket. “I have $2.37,” he said. “Can I please look at them?”

The shop owner smiled and whistled. Out of the kennel came Lady, who ran down the aisle of his shop followed by five teeny, tiny balls of fur.

One puppy was lagging considerably behind. Immediately, the little boy singled out the lagging, limping puppy and said, “What’s wrong with that little dog?”

The shop owner explained that the veterinarian had examined the little puppy and had discovered it didn’t have a hip socket. It would always limp. It would always be lame.

The little boy became excited. “That is the puppy that I want to buy.”

 

The shop owner said, “No, you don’t want to buy that little dog. If you really want him, I’ll give him to you.”

The little boy got quite upset. He looked straight into the store owner’s eyes, pointing his finger, and said,

“I don’t want you to give him to me. That little dog is worth as much as all the other dogs, and I’ll pay full price. In fact, I’ll give you $2.37 now and 50 cents a month until I have him paid for.”

The shop owner countered, “You really don’t want to buy this little dog. He will never be able to run and jump and play with you like the other puppies.”

 

To his surprise, the little boy reached down and rolled up his pant leg to reveal a badly twisted, crippled left leg supported by a big metal brace. He looked up at the shop owner and softly replied, “Well, I don’t run so well myself and the little puppy will need someone who understands!”

title: Race of Life
content:
While riding my bike, I noticed a man in front of me, about half a mile away. I noticed the man was traveling at a speed lower than me. So, I decided to overtake him. I had about a mile to go on the road before turning off.

So, I started cycling faster and faster with every block. I was gaining on him just a little bit. Within minutes, I was about 50 yards behind him, So I gathered all my strength and tried hard to overtake him, and finally, I was ahead of him. It was just like the last lap of the marathon.

And finally, I caught up with him and passed him by. Within, I felt like a winner, “I won.” At the same time, he had no clue that we were in a race.

After I passed him, I realized that I had been so focused on competing against him that I had missed my turn, had gone nearly six blocks past it, and had to turn around and go all back.

Isn’t that what happens in life? We spend most of our time competing with neighbors, friends, and family, trying to outperform or be in front of them. At the same time, you were never in the race with them.

We use most of our time and energy in competition, and instead of reaching our destination, we miss out on our paths to our destinies.

 

Moral of the story:

Unhealthy competition is a continuous process, a never-ending cycle, A race of life. No matter what you do, someone will always be ahead of you: someone with a better everything: a better job, a nicer car, wealth, more education, a prettier wife, a more handsome husband, good children, etc.

 

Feel grateful for what life has offered you, your height, weight, and personality. Dress well & wear it proudly! Stay focused on your path and live a healthy life. There’s no competition in DESTINY. Run your RACE of life and wish others WELL!

title: Rats swim for their life
content: There was a laboratory experiment where rats were dropped into jars of water. If the jar were left in darkness, the rat would swim for just over three minutes and then give up and drown. If there was a ray of light shining into the jar, the rats could keep swimming for 36 hours! That's a powerful illustration of the power of hope. If we "cast a vision... and paint a picture of their future success" for people, it will give them a great source of encouragement and motivation.

title: REMEMBER ME?
content:
I’m the fellow who goes into a restaurant, sits down patiently, and waits while the waitresses do everything but take my order.

I’m the fellow who goes into a department store and stands quietly while the sales clerks finish their little chitchat.

I’m the fellow who goes into a reception room on time for a business appointment and stands by the desk while the receptionist finishes her personal phone call.

Yes, you might say, I’m a good guy. But do you know who else I am?

I’m the fellow who never comes back. It amuses me to see you spending money every year to try to get me back to your company when I was there in the first place, and all you had to do to keep me was to show me a little courtesy.

 

Remember, without the customer, there is no need for you.

Without the customer, there will be no sales.

Without sales, there is business.

Without a business, there is no paycheck.

So, remember ME.

title: Rich Devos
content:
1. If you think it’s impossible, it isn’t.
  2. If you think you know everything, you don’t
  3. If you think you are alone, you’re not.

The founder of Amway, Rich DeVos, was in need of a heart transplant.  After time passed, he received his heart transplant.

He later had dinner with the lady that gave him her heart.

So you say, that’s impossible, you can’t give your heart then still be alive.

This lady needed a lung transplant.  Sometimes, with a lung transplant, it is better that the lung and heart go together.  So, she received a lung and heart transplant from someone else.  That then made her heart become available.

Her heart goes to Rich DeVos.

 

Isn't that an absolutely amazing story? I share that story with you because it is important that you understand:

  1. If you think it’s impossible, it isn’t.
  2. If you think you know everything, you don’t
  3. If you think you are alone, you’re not.

title: Rotten Attitudes
content:
A critical spirit.

Fred and Martha were driving home after a church service.

“Fred,” Martha asked, “did you notice that the pastor’s sermon was kind of weak today?” “No, not really,” answered Fred.  “Well, did you hear that the choir was flat?”  “No, I didn’t,” he responded.  “Well, you certainly must have noticed that young couple and their children right in front of us, with all the noise and commotion they made the whole service!”  “I’m sorry, dear, but no, I didn’t.”  Finally, in disgust, Martha said, “Honestly, Fred, I don’t know why you even bother to go to church.”

 

POINT:

When someone on the team has a critical spirit, everybody knows it because everyone on the team can do no right.

Common rotten attitudes that ruin a team

title: Rule of 5
content:
I’m going to tell you about my Rule of 5

Also, see God created story (under Stories: John told that before he walked through Rule of 5)

 

  • Look at your neighbor and tell them you are about to learn something.
  • In fact, look back at them and say why do you think I brought you here. 
     
  • Let me illustrate for you the Rule of 5:
    • If I have a tree in my back yard.
    • And I had an axe.  I picked up the axe, go over to the tree.
    • I take the axe and swing 5 times against the tree
    • (SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK)
  • Next day I pick up the axe, go to the same tree and smack it 5x.
    • (SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK)
  • Next day I go to my backyard, pick up the axe, go to the tree and smack it 5X
    • (SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK)
  • Next day go to my backyard, pick up the axe, go to the tree and smack it 5X
    • (SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK)
  • ENCOURAGE CROWD PARTICIPATION
  • Go to my backyard, pick up the axe, go to the tree and smack it 5X
    • (SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK, SMACK)

 

  • If every day you go to the tree, pick up the axe and smack it 5X, what is going to happen to the tree?
  • If it’s a big tree it may take a couple years since you are only smacking it 5X.
  • If it’s a smaller tree it may only take a couple months.

 

  • The rule of 5 teaches us the essentials of success:

 

  1. You must know what you want to accomplish it.
    • In this story the man wanted to cut down the tree.
    • All success begins with knowing the goal.
  2. You have to have the right tools.
    • In the story he had an axe.  But what would happen if he didn’t have the right tool?
    • What would have happened if he picked up a baseball instead of an axe?  And when to the tree.
    • He would have put in a lot of effort and time, but that tree would not fall.
  3. You have to focus.
    • Everyday he picked up the axe and he went to the same tree.  He focused.
    • Some people would pick up the axe on day 1 go to one tree
    • Then day 2 he goes to another tree.
    • Then day 3 he goes to another tree.
    • He would never knock the tree down, he just gonna have a lot of scaring on trees.
  4. You have to be consistent
    • You noticed everyday he picked up the axe and hit the tree.
    • Everyday, not every other day.  EVERYDAY
    • When you are consistent you don’t have to do things all day, you just have to do them consistently.
  5. Stay with the task until the goal is accomplished.

 

Now let’s compare Rule of 5 to your team performance.

Rule of 5 will work in any area of life, team goals or tasks.

title: Sel Not Spel
content:
YOU WILL NEED TO SHOW THE CLIENT THIS STORY.  IT IS A VISUAL EXERCISE.  SO EITHER PRINT A COPY FOR EACH PERSON OR SHOW IT ON THE SCREEN/OVERHEAD PROJECTOR.  NOTICE ALL THE MISSPELLED WORDS (THAT IS INTENTIONAL).

 

It said that a recently hired salesman wrote his first sales report to the home office after working in

his territory the first week. It shocked the sales manager because he suddenly realized that he had hired someone who was illiterate.

 

Here’s what the report said: “I went and seen this outfit which ain’t never bot nothin from us befour and I sole em a good order. Now I’m movin on to Nu Yourk.”  The manager was in a panic. But before he could get hold of the salesman to fire him, he received a second report. It said, “I done been hear fer too days and sole them haff a millyon.”

 

Then the manager was really confused. He couldn’t keep an illiterate salesman, but he couldn’t fire a salesman who had outsold everyone else on the sales force. So he did what every good middle manager does: he dumped the problem in the lap of the company’s president.

 

The next morning, everyone in the sales department was amazed to see the salesman’s two letters on the bulletin board along with the following memo from the president: “We bin spendin weigh two much time tryin to spel in stead of tryin to sel. Lets all try to get our sails up. Reed these too letters from hour best salsman. He’s doin a grate job and all you shud go out and do like he done.”

title: Share a secret or the vision with people
content:
Two men went ice fishing, they cut a hole in the ice, baited the line, and dropped the line in.

They sat there for 3 hours but not one bite.

 

A little boy came to fish and sat between them.

He drilled a hole, baited his line, and almost instantly caught a fish.

He repeated the process, and bam another fish.

In a matter of an hour, he had a dozen fish.

 

One old man said, son, what’s your secret?

The little boy mumbled a reply, but the old man didn’t understand him.  So he said, Young man, take your gum out & repeat that.

He noticed a big wad in the little boy’s cheek.  The boy took the wad out and said you must warm the worms.

 

THE POINT:

  • Share the vision or secret with your team.
  • Show them the big picture
  • You will be surprised by how they respond with gratitude and appreciation.
  • It’s an act of Inclusion.
  • It’s an act to let them partake in success.
  • When you do this, you are bound to improve your team morale and individual self-esteem.

title: Silent Treatment
content:
A man and his wife were having some problems at home and were giving each other the silent treatment. Suddenly, the man realized that the next day he would need his wife to wake him at 5.00 am for an early morning business flight.  Not wanting to be the first to break the silence (and lose), he wrote on a piece of paper, “Please wake me at 5.00 am.” He left it where he knew she would find it.

The next morning, the man woke up, only to discover it was 9.00 am and he had missed the flight.  Furious, he was about to go and see why his wife hadn’t wakened him when he noticed a piece of paper by the bed. The paper said, “It is 5.00 am. Wake up.”

 

PONDER AND CONSIDER

Probably at one time or another, you have been either on the giving or receiving end of a silent treatment, otherwise known as the cold shoulder. What are you saying by not saying anything at all?

title: Stay out of The Dean’s Office
content:
One night four college kids stayed out late, partying and having a good time. They paid no mind to the test they had scheduled for the next day and didn’t study. In the morning, they hatched a plan to get out of taking their test. They covered themselves with grease and dirt and went to the Dean’s office. Once there, they said they had been to a wedding the previous night and on the way back they got a flat tire and had to push the car back to campus.

The Dean listened to their tale of woe and thought. He offered them a retest three days later. They thanked him and accepted his offer.

 

When the test day arrived, they went to the Dean. The Dean put them all in separate rooms for the test. They were fine with this since they had all studied hard. Then they saw the test. It had 2 questions.

 

1) Your Name __________ (1 Points)

2) Which tire burst? __________ (99 Points)


Options – (a) Front Left (b) Front Right (c) Back Left (d) Back Right

 

The lesson: always be responsible and make wise decisions.

title: Stone Mason
content:
Here is an old story of the stonemasons. A stranger walks by a construction site and comes upon a stonemason. When the stranger asks what the mason is doing, he replies, “I’m laying stones.” The next day the stranger strolls by again and sees a different mason at work. When the stranger asks him what he’s doing, the mason replies, “I’m building a wall.” On the third day, the man sees yet another mason at work and again asks what the mason is doing. With great joy in his voice, the worker replies, “I’m building a cathedral!”

 

It’s a corny story, but I love it for so many reasons. First, each mason accomplished something. Day by day and stone by stone, the project progressed because of their efforts. Second, this tale speaks to the power of perspective: For the first mason, the assignment was a menial task; for the second, it was a manageable project; for the third, it was a marvelous goal. That parable, to me, perfectly captures the power of achievement.

title: Story of the Pot Roast!
content:
LONG STORY

 

As each year begins to wind down, it’s natural for many of us to take inventory of the past year and start thinking about the changes we hope to make in the year to come.

 

As I recently thought about what it takes to create change, I remembered a story I heard a long time ago.

 

The Story of the Pot Roast

A young woman was hosting a dinner party for her friends and served a delicious pot roast.  One of her friends enjoyed it so much that she asked for the recipe, and the young woman wrote it down for her.

 

Upon looking over the recipe, her friend inquired, “Why do you cut both ends off the roast before it is prepared and put in the pan?” The young woman replied, “I don’t know. I cut the ends off because I learned this recipe from my mom and that was the way she had always done it.”

 

Her friend’s question got the young woman thinking and so the next day she called her mom to ask her: “Mom, when we make the pot roast, why do we cut off and discard the ends before we set it in the pan and season it?” Her mom quickly replied, “That is how your grandma always did it and I learned the recipe from her.”

 

Now the young woman was really curious, so she called her elderly grandma and asked her the same question: “Grandma, I often make the pot roast recipe that I learned from mom and she learned from you. Why do you cut the ends off the roast before you prepare it?”

 

The grandmother thought for a while, since it had been years since she made the roast herself, and then replied, “I cut them off because the roast was always bigger than the pan I had back then. I had to cut the ends off to make it fit.”

I love this story because I think this is true for so many of the things we do in life. We have been doing them for so long that we rarely stop and question the rationality behind them anymore.

 

Gaining awareness

As this story demonstrates, for any change to take place, the first step is to gain awareness of what we are doing. Until we gain awareness, we cannot begin to question the relevance of the thought, behavior, or action that we are taking…can we?

 

For most of us, we learned our behaviors a long time ago (or thoughts and beliefs were instilled in us a long time ago) and maybe there is a different or better way to do or see things today?

 

However, most of us keep replaying the same behaviors—and telling ourselves the same stories—on auto-pilot, again and again and again.

 

“If you always do what you’ve always done, you’ll always get what you’ve always got.”

 

Remember that saying? It is my personal belief that if you truly want to create change, the first step is to take the time to actually become aware of what you’ve always done!
