This means that we need to analyze and evaluate our current actions and behaviors, as well as our current thoughts, (including the stories we continuously tell ourselves) in order to create change.

Here are some questions that you can ponder…

 

What are the things you’ve been doing for years that may no longer be relevant today?

 

Maybe you do these things because, at one point, someone told you to do them that way. Or maybe you do them simply because it’s been so long that you can’t remember not doing them.

 

Where did these actions and thoughts originate? And, more importantly, are they still accurate and the best choices for you now?

 

For example, maybe you start every morning with coffee or end every evening with wine. I often see clients who simply do this out of a long-time habit but when they actually evaluate their need/desire for that behavior, they discover that they feel far more energetic, relaxed, or healthier today by making a different choice.

Or maybe you witnessed your parents worrying about money and you too worry about money, despite the fact that your bank account and spending habits actually do not warrant that concern.

 

What have I believed about myself since I was young that actually may not be true any longer?

 

Maybe in the past you always got sick in the winters, or feared speaking in public, or had a hard time eating sweets in moderation. And now every time one of those situations arise, you tell yourself what has happened in the past rather than evaluating if it is actually still true in the present.

 

Maybe it is, and the awareness can then help initiate improvement. But maybe it’s simply not true any longer!

 

I am personally working on not referring to myself as a perfectionist anymore! Yes, I can still set high standards for myself, but the truth is, I have also let go of a lot of those standards and I am continuously working on a kinder and gentler way of relating to myself.

 

What are the “stories” I still tell myself that simply are not relevant today?

 

I often hear statements from my clients such as: “I have no self-control” or “I never accomplish anything you tell me to do” or “I can’t stick with any healthy eating plan for long.” The interesting part is that oftentimes the statements they are making are not even accurate with what they are doing!

 

For example, a recent client listed three accomplishments, and then remembered the one task she didn’t get to, and the story she told me (and herself!) became: “I never get anything done.”

Really?!

 

Cultivating change

Answering these question and, thus, bringing awareness to our current thoughts and behaviors can help us to live more in the present, as well as to guide us to make the changes we hope to see in the future.

 

In what areas of your life are you still “cutting the ends off your pot roast?”

title: Success On Your Terms
content:
I was recently reminded of a commencement address delivered by former Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, Anna Quindlen in 2002 at Sarah Lawrence College. She encouraged the graduates to own their dreams by saying, “When I quit The New York Times to be a full-time mother, the voices of the world said I was nuts. When I quit the paper again to be a novelist, they said I was nuts again. But if success is not on your own terms, if it looks good to the world but does not feel good in your soul, it is not success at all.”

Did you catch that? I don’t want you to miss this…

 

If your success looks good to the world but doesn’t feel good in your soul, it is not success at all.

title: The Blind Girl
content:
There was a blind girl who hated herself purely for the fact she was blind. The only person she didn’t hate was her loving boyfriend, as he was always there for her. She said that if she could only see the world, she would marry him.

One day, someone donated a pair of eyes to her – now she could see everything, including her boyfriend. Her boyfriend asked her, “Now that you can see the world, will you marry me?”

The girl was shocked when she saw that her boyfriend was blind too, and refused to marry him. Her boyfriend walked away in tears and later wrote a letter to her saying:

“Just take care of my eyes dear.”

 

Moral of the story:

When our circumstances change, so does our mind. Some people may not be able to see the way things were before, and might not be able to appreciate them.

title: The Butterfly Struggles
content:
A man found a cocoon of a butterfly.

One day, a small opening appeared. He sat and watched the butterfly for several hours as it struggled to force its body through that little hole.

 

Until it suddenly stopped making any progress and looked like it was stuck.

So the man decided to help the butterfly. He took a pair of scissors and snipped off the remaining bit of the cocoon. The butterfly then emerged easily, although it had a swollen body and small, shriveled wings.

 

The man didn’t think anything of it and sat there waiting for the wings to enlarge to support the butterfly. But that didn’t happen. The butterfly spent the rest of its life unable to fly, crawling around with tiny wings and a swollen body.

 

Despite the kind heart of the man, he didn’t understand that the restricting cocoon and the struggle needed by the butterfly to get itself through the small opening were God’s way of forcing fluid from the body of the butterfly into its wings. To prepare itself for flying once it was out of the cocoon.

 

Moral of the story:

Our struggles in life develop our strengths. Without struggles, we never grow and never get stronger, so it’s important for us to tackle challenges on our own and not rely on help from others.

title: The Leader
content:
I love the story of a group of neighborhood boys who built a tree house and formed their own club. When the grown-ups were told who had been selected for which office, they were astonished to hear that a four-year-old had been elected president.

 

“That boy must be a born leader,” one dad observed. “How did it happen that all you bigger boys voted for him?” “Well, you see, Dad,” his son replied, “he can’t be a secretary because he doesn’t know how to read or write. He couldn’t be treasurer because he can’t count. He would never do good for sergeant at arms because he’s too little to throw anybody out. If we didn’t choose him for anything, he’d feel bad. So we made him president.”

 

THE POINT:

Real life, of course, doesn’t work that way. You don’t become an effective leader by default. You must be intentional. And you must work from your strengths.

title: The Legion of the 6 Blind Men
content:
The Legion of the 6 Blind Men and Their Examination of An Elephant:

1st man touched the side of the elephant and said it was very much like a wall.

2nd man touched the elephant’s tusk and said it was very much like a spear.

3rd man took the elephant’s trunk in his hand and commented it was very much like a snake.

4th man, embracing one of the legs, commented that it’s very much like a tree.

5th man, feeling and touching the elephant’s ear, said even a blind man can tell it’s very much like a fan.

6th man grabbed a hold of the tail and said this elephant is really very much like a rope.

Then the 6 men went home, each one satisfied that he understood what an elephant looked like.

This tells it all, the fact that 6 people could be in an environment and come away with 6 different conclusions.


 

Do you see things from A Singular Perspective?

 

“If the only tool you have is a hammer, you tend to see every problem as a nail.” -Larry Stephens

title: The Obstacle in our Path
content:
There once was a very wealthy and curious king. This king had a huge boulder placed in the middle of a road. Then he hid nearby to see if anyone would try to remove the gigantic rock from the road.

 

The first people to pass by were some of the king’s wealthiest merchants and courtiers. Rather than moving it, they simply walked around it. A few loudly blamed the King for not maintaining the roads. Not one of them tried to move the boulder.

 

Finally, a peasant came along. His arms were full of vegetables. When he got near the boulder, rather than simply walking around it as the others had, the peasant put down his load and tried to move the stone to the side of the road. It took much effort, but he finally succeeded.

 

The peasant gathered up his load and was ready to go on his way when he saw a purse lying in the road where the boulder had been. The peasant opened the purse. The purse was stuffed full of gold coins and a note from the king. The king’s note said the purse’s gold was a reward for moving the boulder from the road.

 

Moral of the story:

Every obstacle we come across in life gives us an opportunity to improve our circumstances, and whilst the lazy complain, the others are creating opportunities through their kind hearts, generosity, and willingness to get things done.

title: The Parrot
content:
I heard this story about this lady who bought a parrot at a store.  She was lonely, so she bought a parrot to talk with her.

 

She got the parrot home and put him in his cage, but after setting it up, she realized the parrot didn’t talk.  So the next day, she returned to the store and told the store owner that the parrot didn’t speak.  He said, you know, you may need to buy a ladder because parrots like to climb and get exercise.

So she got that, but the parrot still didn’t talk.

 

So the next day, she returned to the store and said he didn’t talk.  The store owner said you may need to get him a swing. Parrots like to swing and go back and forth, which puts them in a good mood.  So she got that and went back home.  But the parrot still didn’t talk.

 

So the next day, she returned to the store and said he didn’t talk.  He said, you need a mirror; parrots like to look at themselves.  So she got a mirror.  The parrot just looked at himself, swung, and climbed, but he didn’t talk.

 

So the next day, she returned to the store and said the parrot died.  The store owner said he died; how terrible. He said, did he say anything before he died?

 

She said yes, and he asked, “Don’t they sell food down there?”  I’m hungry.

 

I know all kinds of people in their spiritual lives; they have ladders, mirrors, swings, and a lot of stuff.  But they don’t understand that less is more. You have to go for the simple, go for the true.  Feed your soul.  Feed yourself spiritually, feed your dreams, and provide your goals with action.

title: The power of withholding rewards
content:
This story illustrates the power of withholding rewards.

An older couple had been at a campground for a couple of days when a family arrived at the site next to them. As soon as their sport-utility vehicle came to a stop, the couple and their three kids piled out. One child hurriedly unloaded ice chests, backpacks, and other items while the other two quickly put up tents. The site was ready in fifteen minutes.

The older couple was amazed. “You folks sure do work great together,” the elderly gentleman told the dad admiringly.

“You just need a system,” replied the dad. “Nobody goes to the bathroom until camp’s set up.”

title: The Power of Words
content:
Good opener to go with DISC or ECFC training

 

Prop: Get a cigarette to act like you will light it, then say:

 

What? Y’all think smoking kills? Let me tell you something. Do you know that the amount of people dying from diabetes is three times as many people dying from smoking? Yet if I pulled a Snickers bar, nobody would say anything. Do you know that the leading cause of lung cancer is actually not a cigarette? It's your DNA. You could smoke for years, and nothing would ever happen to you. This whole world against smoking is to restrict the farming of tobacco.

 

I use these arguments, even though I just made them up, with a group of my friends. And the results? Five of them believed what I said. Two of them started smoking.

 

Words, when said and articulated in the right way, can change someone's mind. They can alter someone's belief. You have the power to bring someone from the slums of life and make a successful person out of them or destroy someone's happiness using only your words.

 

Does that seem a bit too good to be true? A simple choice of words can make a difference between someone accepting or denying your message. You can have a very beautiful thing to say, but say it in the wrong words and it's gone.

 

When my son was 4 yrs old I caught him writing on the carpet with a sharpie. I screamed hey are stupid, don’t do that again.  The very next day, I walked in and he was writing in the carpet again but this time he was looking at me, sort of like in defiance. This time, I kneeled down and said, son, you are a big boy now. Big boys don’t write on the carpet.  He never did it again.

 

The first time, I attacked his ego. No one wants their ego hurt. The second time I complimented his ego. Everyone wants their ego stroked.

title: The Right Place
content:
A mother and a baby camel were lying around under a tree.

Then the baby camel asked, “Why do camels have humps?”

 

The mother camel considered this and said, “We are desert animals so we have the humps to store water so we can survive with very little water.”

 

The baby camel thought for a moment then said, “Ok…why are our legs long and our feet rounded?”

The mama replied, “They are meant for walking in the desert.”

 

The baby paused. After a beat, the camel asked, “Why are our eyelashes long? Sometimes they get in my way.”

The mama responded, “Those long thick eyelashes protect your eyes from the desert sand when it blows in the wind.

 

The baby thought and thought. Then he said, “I see. So the hump is to store water when we are in the desert, the legs are for walking through the desert and these eyelashes protect my eyes from the desert then why in the Zoo?”

 

The Lesson: Skills and abilities are only useful if you are in the right place at the right time. Otherwise, they go to waste.

title: There are 2 sides to every story
content:
A teacher teaching math in a class of 6-year-olds.
asked a boy named Adi.

 

” Adi, if I give you two mangos and another two mangos. How many mangoes will you have?
He answered “Five mangoes”.

She was surprised by his reply but she tried again. Now this time she uses her fingers to make him count with her.


“Ok Adi, look if I give you One, Two. Two mangoes and another one-two. Two mangoes. How many mangoes will you have?”


He again answered ” Five mangoes”

This time she gets really annoyed by his answer but she controlled her anger and remembered that his mother once told her that he likes the strawberries. So, she tried this.


“Ok Adi, If I give you two strawberries and another two strawberries. Now, how many strawberries do you have?”
“I would have four strawberries.”

 

She felt relieved that he was back on track. So, again she asked him.
“Now tell me, Adi, If I give you two mangoes and another two mangoes, how many mangoes do you have?”
He answered,  "Teacher, Five mangoes.”


The teacher outburst in anger ”How can you have five mangoes if I give you four mangoes?”


“Teacher, because I already have one mango in my bag.”


Complete silence. The teacher calms down and regrets her anger.


 

Moral of the Story:

Two sides to every story. Never judge others. We should not make a decision for others without knowing their point of view. We make the decision on the basis of what is logical rightness i.e. What is the obvious answer.  But we don’t try to understand the practical rightness i.e. What is the actual truth.

title: There is a reason it is hard to have back-to-back championships
content:
There is a reason it is hard to have back-to-back championships.  They can’t handle the perks of their first championship.  They start to show their trophy off, they read the newspaper and they enjoy the perks of their success.  Then all of a sudden they begin to back off.  You see the perks that come with the first championship which are the hindrances that come with the next one.  When a team wins their first championship, they don’t get the next one free.  That’s why this price thing is huge, the price is always going to be paid.  You must constantly pay the price.

 

Cal Ripken is in baseball HOF.  He wasn’t the best hitter.  He wasn’t the best fielder.  He was the best player, but he was the most consistent.  He played 2,632 consecutive games.  Wow, he showed up every day.  Not everyone shows up every day, but he did.

 

Sports Story:

The great QBs in the NFL after they throw an interception, can’t wait to get the ball again so they can throw another pass.  Because they know they are better than that.

You see, the QBs that are not so good, don’t want the ball again.

title: There was a little girl in school
content:
There was a little girl in school on show and tell day, who was talking about Jonah in the belly of the whale.  The teacher told her that there is no way possible for a person to live in the belly of a whale. The little girl said, it’s true, my bible tells me it is so. The teacher said no, it can’t happen. The girl looked puzzled at the teacher and said, “Well when I get to heaven I’m gonna ask Jonah.”

 

The teacher looked back at her said asked, what if you go to hell”. The little girl replied, “Then you ask him”.

title: There was a man who lost his job
content:
There was a man who lost his job, so he got unemployment. After a few weeks, that ran out.

Then rent came due, but he had no money.

Then the car note came due, but he was out of money.

Then he needed food, but he was out of money.

 

So he decided to go to Job Corp for a job, but they told him there were no jobs available.

So he went to the Employment office, but they told him no jobs with his skills were available.

So he went to the Salvation Army for assistance, but they told him they could not help.

So he went to the United Way for assistance, but again, they told him no assistance was available.

Finally, he went to the Social Security office for help, but they said there was nothing they could do.

 

Depressed and feeling dejected, he decided to commit suicide. He figured if he did that, at least his family would get his life insurance money, but he knew that wouldn’t work. He went down his list and said well, the only thing I didn’t do is ask Jesus. He realized that J for Job Corp, E for Employment office, S for Salvation Army, U for United Way, and S for Social Security Office spells JESUS.

 

If we look at Jesus in our time of need, we will find he will provide all the assistance we need and want.

 

Job Corp

Employment Office

Salvation Army

United Way

Social Security Office

title: They Walk Among Us
content:
Just a few short funny snippets to add to a program

John Maxwell

 

As I got into the growth environment, I realized that I sometimes may have to leave a lot of friends behind.

Here are a few funny stories that remind me: “They walk among us.”  See if you can relate.

 

  1. One day, I was walking along the beach with some friends, and one of them shouted look at that dead bird.  One of them looked up in the sky and said, where?  THEY WALK AMONG US.
  2. While looking at a house, my brother asked the real estate agent which direction was north because he didn’t want the sun waking him up every morning.  She replied, “Does the sun rise in the north?”  When my brother explained that the sun rises in the east and has for some time.  She replied, “I can’t keep up with that stuff.”   THEY WALK AMONG US.
  3. My sister has a life-saving tool in her car that will allow her to cut the seatbelt if she gets trapped.  She keeps it in the trunk.

       THEY WALK AMONG US.

  4. I used to work on a technical support hotline for a 24/7 call center.  One day, I got a call from an individual asking what hours we opened; I said the number you dialed is open 24 hours, 7 days a week. He responded in that Eastern or Pacific time.

       THEY WALK AMONG US.

 5. I couldn’t find my luggage at the airport baggage area, so I went to the lost luggage office.  I told the woman that my baggage never showed up.  She smiled and told me, “no worries, I’m a trained professional, I can help you.  You are in good hands.”  Then she asked me if my plane arrived yet?  THEY WALK AMONG US.

 

And some people wonder why they should make some new friends.

title: Thinking Outside of the Box
content:
In a small Italian town, hundreds of years ago, a small business owner owed a large sum of money to a loan shark. The loan shark was a very old, unattractive-looking guy who just so happened to fancy the business owner’s daughter.

He decided to offer the businessman a deal that would completely wipe out the debt he owed him. However, the catch was that we would only wipe out the debt if he could marry the businessman’s daughter.

Needless to say, this proposal was met with a look of disgust.

The loan shark said that he would place two pebbles into a bag, one white and one black.

The daughter would then have to reach into the bag and pick out a pebble. If it was black, the debt would be wiped, but the loan shark would then marry her. If it was white, the debt would also be wiped, but the daughter wouldn’t have to marry the loan shark.

 

Standing on a pebble-strewn path in the businessman’s garden, the loan shark bent over and picked up two pebbles.

 

Whilst he was picking them up, the daughter noticed that he’d picked up two black pebbles and placed them both into the bag.

 

He then asked the daughter to reach into the bag and pick one.

The daughter naturally had three choices as to what she could have done:

  1. Refuse to pick a pebble from the bag.
  2. Take both pebbles out of the bag and expose the loan shark for cheating.
  3. Pick a pebble from the bag, fully knowing it was black, and sacrifice herself for her father’s freedom.

 

She drew out a pebble from the bag, and before looking at it ‘accidentally’ dropped it into the midst of the other pebbles. She said to the loan shark;

“Oh, how clumsy of me. Never mind, if you look into the bag for the one that is left, you will be able to tell which pebble I picked.”

The pebble left in the bag is obviously black, and seeing as the loan-shark didn’t want to be exposed, he had to play along as if the pebble the daughter dropped was white, and clear her father’s debt.

 

Moral of the story:

It’s always possible to overcome a tough situation through out-of-the-box thinking, and not give in to the only options you think you have to pick from.

title: Thomas Edison was practically deaf
content:
Thomas Edison was practically deaf.  When hearing aids were developed, Henry Ford rushed out to buy the most expensive pair on the market for Edison.  In fact, he could barely hear so when he was in a group of people, he would normally sit there or walk out and go into his lab to work because he couldn’t hear what they were saying.  After Ford purchased them, he went down to Ft Myers to give them to Edison. He said, I just purchased the greatest thing for you: these new hearing aids.

He said, here, put them on to try them out.

 

Edison looked at Henry Ford and said, “Oh no, I don’t want those. He said if I start wearing those, I will have to start listening to all these conversations and opinions and mess up my work. Oh no, I would rather keep it just like it is now.”

title: Thomas Edison was the guest
content:
Thomas Edison was the guest of the governor of North Carolina when the politician complimented him on his creative genius.

“I am not a great inventor,” countered Edison.

“But you have more than a thousand patents to your credit,” the governor stated.

 

“Yes, but the only invention I can really claim as absolutely original is the phonograph,” Edison replied.

 

“I’m afraid I don’t understand what you mean,” the governor remarked.

“Well,” explained Edison, “I guess I’m an awfully good sponge. I absorb ideas from every course I can and put them to practical use. Then I improve them until they become of some value. The ideas which I use are mostly the ideas of other people who don’t develop them themselves.”

What a remarkable description of someone who used teachability to expand his talent! That is what a talent-plus person does. That is what all of us should strive to do.

title: Three old sisters
content:
3 old sisters were living together; they were 96, 94, and 92 years old.

The 96-year-old drew a bath, and she put 1 foot in the water and stopped and said I don’t know whether I was getting in or getting out.

 

The 94-year-old was walking up the stairs, and she said don’t worry, I’ll come to help. We will figure out what you were doing and let you know. She got halfway up the stairs, and she stop, and she said, I don’t know whether I was going up or going down.

 

The 92-year-old was standing at the door, and she said, oh God, I hope I never get like them so forgetful, and then she knocked on wood for good luck. Then she said I’ll come help both of you as soon as I find out who’s at the door.

title: Tiger Woods
content:
Break Away For A Takeaway

 

Do you know the difference between a “comeback story” and a “comeback study”?

 

A “comeback story” is inspirational. You know the plot by heart: a hero falls from grace and battles against great odds just for one more shot at redemption. Comeback stories are a great part of our cultural narrative—we love the idea of someone rebuilding their life, and we love the way those tales leave us feeling inspired.

 

But how often do we hear a great comeback story and do something with that inspiration?

 

That’s what makes a “comeback study” different. A comeback study is when you analyze a great comeback story and look for the lessons within. It’s when you intentionally turn inspiration into action and use that momentary emotion to create lasting momentum.

 

I’m reminded of one of the most significant falls from grace we’ve seen in the last 15 years: an A-list athlete, once believed to be unstoppable, saw everything in his life fall apart as the result of his choices. He lost a marriage, a career, and a place of respect amongst our athletic heroes.

 

His name?

 

Tiger Woods.

 

(PUT ON SCREEN)

Booker T Washington said,

“Success is not where you are; success is what you had to overcome to get where you are.“

 

Now, whether you follow golf or not, you know the story of Tiger Woods; he took a big fall from grace.  His life fell apart; his career fell apart; his marriage fell apart.  He had to go into sex rehab, multiple injuries, and a run-in with the law over prescription drugs.  He just was not the same, clean Tiger everybody had come to know of.

 

Maybe you’ve heard that he’s made a return to competitive golf after a long road back. While some people continue to look at him with suspicion—because a fall like Tiger’s often leaves a lot of people cold—there are others who have extended him a hand of grace. It is amazing that he is coming back.  People did not look at him the same, golfers didn’t look at him the same, sponsors left him, and the general public didn’t accept him.

 

I believe people are rooting for Tiger now because they see some of themselves in him and want to be given a little grace if they fall. (WE ALL DO)  We love to see people come back like we see Tiger Woods.  It is almost as if humanity is cheering for him to come back.  You may not get back to where you were, but you are coming back.

 

No matter who you are or what you do, Tiger can teach you a few things about making a comeback. His story can teach us about giving others some grace and not holding a person’s past “forever” against him.

 

4 LESSONS  I LEARNED:

  1. When you fall, it takes a long time to get back.
  2. You fall a lot faster than you rise.
  3. The only way you come back is through humility.  He is now reachable.
  4. He may never get back to where he was positionally, but where he is coming back to now will allow him to be loved more than he ever was before.  That’s because he is taking a pathway that people can identify with, they can value and appreciate.

 

WHY:

Because we all want to be given grace, be loved, and appreciated. We all have a need to be accepted, even if we put up our shield that it doesn’t matter.  Inside your heart, when you have that silent moment with yourself, you wonder why people don’t like you, why they don’t see it your way or appreciate your work.

 

Tiger Woods has earned:

82 PGA Tour wins

15 Majors

$120 million in winnings

$1.5 billion in endorsements

The first PIP Award

 

He's launched his own:

Golf courses

Mini golf courses

Restaurant

Live event series

Golf clubs

Golf simulator

Foundation, donating more than $12 million

 

In March 2022, he was inducted into the World Golf Hall of Fame.

 

NOW you know the difference between a “comeback story” and a “comeback study.”

title: To Rope an Elephant
content:
As a man was passing the elephants, he suddenly stopped, confused by the fact that these huge creatures were being held by only a small rope tied to their front leg. No chains, no cages. It was obvious that the elephants could, at any time, break away from their bonds but for some reason, they did not.

 

He saw a trainer nearby and asked why these animals just stood there and made no attempt to get away. “Well,” the trainer said, “when they are very young and much smaller we use the same size rope to tie them and, at that age, it’s enough to hold them. As they grow up, they are conditioned to believe they cannot break away. They believe the rope can still hold them, so they never try to break free.”

 

The man was amazed. These animals could at any time break free from their bonds but because they believed they couldn’t, they were stuck right where they were.

 

Like the elephants, how many of us go through life hanging onto a belief that we cannot do something, simply because we failed at it once before?

 

Failure is part of learning; we should never give up the struggle in life.  No matter how much the world tries to hold you back, always continue with the belief that what you want to achieve is possible. Believing you can become successful is the most important step in actually achieving it.

title: Tourist
content:
A group of tourists are visiting a European village.  They were really enjoying themselves.  They were feeling very nostalgic.

As they were walking through the village, they came upon an old man sitting on the sidewalk.

So, they started talking to him, they asked him if he lived there. They said we love this little village. It has been great.

He said yes, I’ve lived here all my life.

 

Then they got excited and said we have a question for you.

Have any great babies been born here?

The old man shook his head and said no only babies.

 

Today in this country, in this city only babies are being born. Those babies that are being born are right here in this room.

See greatness comes from you teaching, grooming, and implanting values in those babies. And living those values.

They are not born that way.  We make them GREAT.

 

Talent is a gift, GREATNESS is a choice….

title: TRUE STORIES:
content:
1. The British Civil Service in 1803 asked for a man to stand on the cliffs of Dover with a spyglass and he was instructed to ring a bell if he saw Napoleon coming.  That was in 1803, the job was finally abolished in 1945.

 

  1. In the British military, they were handling a field cannon with 6 men, but they could only figure a job for 5 men, so they studied the history of manning the cannon and found out that hundreds of years before the 6th man was to hold the horse and they were still having the 6th man.

 

  1. The czar in Russia was walking across the Cremlin ground in 1915 and noticed a century (guard) posted in the middle of the ground every day, just standing there in the middle of the ground.  So, he asked, what is he doing out there? But no one knew.  Now that was in 1915. In 1776 when Kathryn The Great was the Czar of Russia was walking across the grounds and noticed a flower.  It was the first flower of the spring and she did not want anyone to step on it, so she said post a century there so nobody would step on that flower.

 

These are all true stories.  True stories of traditions, historical events, comfort zone jobs, and thinking.  Where are you or where is your organization doing things because just because it’s always been done that way? Where are you and where is your organization still in a comfort zone?

 

These stories help when you are talking about doing something because you have always done it that way.

title: Two shoe salesmen
content:
Two shoe salesmen were sent to an island to sell shoes. The first salesman, upon arrival, was shocked to realize that no one wore shoes.  Immediately he sent a telegram to his home office in Chicago saying, “Will return home tomorrow. No one wears shoes.”

The second salesman was thrilled by the same realization. Immediately, he wired the home office in Chicago, saying, “Please send me 10,000 shoes.  Everyone here needs them.”

title: Value
content:
A father said to his daughter “You have graduated with honors, here is a car I bought many years ago. It is pretty old now. But before I give it to you, take it to the used car lot downtown and tell them I want to sell it and see how much they offer you for it.”

The daughter went to the used car lot, returned to her father, and said, “They offered me $1,000 because they said it looks pretty worn out.”

The father said, now “Take it to the pawn shop.” The daughter went to the pawn shop, returned to her father, and said, ”The pawn shop offered only $100 because it is an old car.”

The father asked his daughter to go to a car club now and show them the car. The daughter then took the car to the club, returned, and told her father,” Some people in the club offered $100,000 for it because it’s a Nissan Skyline R34, it's an iconic car and sought by many collectors”

Now the father said this to his daughter, “The right place values you the right way,” If you are not valued, do not be angry, it means you are in the wrong place.

 

Those who know your value are those who appreciate you......

Those who know your value are those who accept you….

Those who know your value are those who try to add value to you…

 

Never stay in a place where no one sees your value.

Never stay in a place where no one sees your value.

 

How do I know if they see my value?

If they accept you for who you are.

If they accept you without trying to change you.

Job: If they offer you what you are worth.

Product/Service: They will pay you for product/service.

You can always do things for no charge.

But you should do things so well, that people are willing to pay double.

 

Never stay in a place where no one sees your value.

title: Value Yourself
content:
A popular speaker started off a seminar by holding up a $20 bill. A crowd of 200 had gathered to hear him speak. He asked, “Who would like this $20 bill?”

 

200 hands went up.

 

He said, “I am going to give this $20 to one of you but first, let me do this.” He crumpled the bill up.

He then asked, “Who still wants it?”

 

All 200 hands were still raised.

 

“Well,” he replied, “What if I do this?” Then he dropped the bill on the ground and stomped on it with his shoes.

He picked it up and showed it to the crowd. The bill was all crumpled and dirty.

 

“Now who still wants it?”

 

All the hands still went up.

 

“My friends, I have just shown you a very important lesson. No matter what I did to the money, you still wanted it because it did not decrease in value. It was still worth $20. Many times in our lives, life crumples us and grinds us into the dirt. We make bad decisions or deal with poor circumstances. We feel worthless. But no matter what has happened or what will happen, you will never lose your value. You are special – Don’t ever forget it!

title: Warren Buffet & AFLAC
content:
I was at an executive leadership conference in New York and Linda Kaplan Thaler(the lady that came up with the Aflac commercials), spoke for 2 hours.  Aflac went to her company to ask for help with company branding.  As they were working on a campaign, one of their employees pronounced it “Aflac”, sounding like a duck and that is how they created that commercial.  Today it is the #5 most recognized name in the world. All because of that stupid duck.

 

After the conference was over, she told us about her time with Warren Buffet.  She said at the event, you would only get 10 minutes with Mr Buffet.  She said, she studied up all about him in preparation for her 10 minutes with him.  She found that Cherry Coke was his favorite drink.  He has made over $11 million with Coke, so no surprise he loves the product.  So as she came into the meeting with him, they reminded her she only had 10 minutes.  As she sat down, she handed him a cherry coke and said, I know I only have 10 minutes but I figured we would start with your favorite beverage.   As he popped the can, he looked at her and said Young lady you can have as much time as you want.  No one has ever started an interview with my favorite beverage and she spent 1.5 hours with him.

 

What was she doing?  She understood that connecting was all about others.  If you want to connect with others, you have to forget yourself.  You have to forget yourself in conversation, you have to forget yourself in speaking/teaching.

title: West Texas rancher had a coming-out party
content:
West TX rancher had a coming out party for his daughter.

I’m talking about a really wealthy guy, he owned: thousands of acres, thousands of head of cattle, many well-producing oil wells, a great big house, and an Olympic size pool.

He invited hundreds of guys to this party, they came from hundreds of miles away.

The party was going well and around midnight the host invited them to his Olympic size swimming pool.

He stocked this swimming pool with water moccasins and alligators.

He said, to the young men, any of you that jump in this pool and swim the length of it, I’ll give you 5,000 acres of my best land.  He said, if you don’t want the land, I’ll give you $1 million in cash.

And he said, if you don’t want that, I will give you the hand of my daughter in marriage.

He said, now I don’t have to tell you fellas this, but it is obvious and everybody should know that she is our only heir. And the one who gets her as a bride will eventually get all of this.

The words were no sooner out of his mouth and there was a loud splash in that pool, followed by an immediate emergence of a strapping young man at the other end of the pool.

He set a world record to swim in that pool.

The host was all excited, so he ran down to greet the young man, who was shaking himself off from that swim.

He said, congratulations, young man, that is absolutely fantastic.

He asked, do you want the 5,000 acres of land, he said, no, sir.

He asked, well do you want the $1 million in cash, he said, no, sir.

He asked, well I assume you want my daughter’s hand in marriage, he said, no sir.

So, the West Texan said, so for crying out loud, what do you want?

The young man said I want to know the name of that young man who pushed me into that swimming pool?

 

Now, we would all agree that he was motivated.

I think we will all agree that there is some confusion about motivation.

 

Law of Consistency says: Motivation gets you going, but discipline keeps you going and growing.

 

Some people ask is motivation permanent?  No, motivation is not permanent, just like a bath is not permanent.  You have to take another one.  Motivation is not permanent just like eating is not permanent, unless you stop eating then your condition will be permanent.

title: What a child can teach you….
content:
I was busy reading my favorite magazine and my little girl was playing around me which was disturbing my reading. So, in order to get me some peace, I tried a trick so as to keep her busy for a little while.

I then took a page out from my magazine which had a printed map on it and made some pieces of the map and handed it over to my little girl.  I then asked her to go into her room put torn pieces together and make a complete map again.

 

After all my tricks played on my little girl, I was convinced that now, I could have the silence to read the magazine without any distractions and it would take her some time to figure it out, meanwhile, the whole day would pass.

But within a couple of minutes, she was standing in front of me with a perfect map in her little hands.  I was amazed as well as confused.

So, I asked her how she did it so quickly and easily.

 

She smiled, looked up at me, and said “Oh, Dad, There is an Actor’s face on the other side of the map. I just tried to make his face completely.”

Then she turned and ran outside to play, leaving me surprised.

 

Moral of the story:

In life, there is always the other aspect of whatever you face. Whenever we come across a difficult or challenging, puzzling situation, just sit back and look at the other side, you will be surprised to see an easy way to handle the problem…

title: What Good is Religion
content:
Norm Lawson tells the story of a rabbi and a soap maker who went for a walk together. The soap maker said, “What good is religion? Look at all the trouble and misery of the world! Still there, even after years—thousands of years—of teaching about goodness and truth and peace. Still there, after all the prayers, sermons, and teachings. If religion is good and true, why should this be?”

 

The rabbi said nothing. They continued walking until he noticed a child playing in the gutter.

Then the rabbi said, “Look at that child. You say that soap makes people clean, but see the dirt on that youngster. Of what good is soap? With all the soap in the world, over all these years, the child is still filthy. I wonder how effective soap is, after all!”

 

The soap maker protested, “But, Rabbi, soap cannot do any good unless it is used!”

“Exactly,” replied the rabbi.

 

USE:

When someone has a limiting belief, especially in religion.

title: When an elephant was very young
content:
When an elephant was very young and weighed only several hundred pounds, it was restricted by having a chain clasped to its leg and connected to a tree or deep stake.  When it tried to move away and learned that it could not break the chain, it limited itself.  It believed that whatever restriction was put on it, even a rope it could have easily broken, was more powerful than it was.

People are similar to elephants.  We often believe that some of the restrictions we may have experienced earlier in life are permanent. Or we have been told we have limitations that we don’t actually possess, and these things are keeping us from taking the journey in life that we long for.

 

These are CHAINS we need to break.

title: Who you are determines how you see others.
content:
Two men went into a hardware store at separate times.  They both had just moved to this new town.

 

One guy walked into the hardware store and asked the keeper a question.  He said, we are new to town and I wanted to know how are the people in the town?  Are they friendly?  Are they warm?

 

The store owner was a very wise man, he asked well how were the people in the town you just came from?  The man replied, “Well they weren’t very friendly at all, so we were excited about moving here, we are hoping that they are friendlier here.”   The store owner replied, “Well I hate to disappoint you but they aren’t very friendly here either.”

 

A couple of hours later, the other guy walks into the store.   He asked the keeper a question.  He said, we are new to town and I wanted to know how are the people in the town, are they friendly, are they warm?

 

The store owner, asked, well how were the people in the town you just came from?

 

The man replied, “We hated to leave the town.  The people were so friendly, so cooperative, we just hated to leave the town, we had great neighbors.”  The hardware store owner smiled and said, I have great news for you, the people in this town are just the same way.”

 

You see, there are people that have destination disease, they just think if they could just move somewhere or meet someone or do this or go there, things would be better.  That all of a sudden their life would change.  That’s why I love this expression, “no matter where you are, THERE YOU ARE.”

title: Why your competition doesn’t need you to fail
content:
Why your competition doesn’t need you to fail, only to hesitate.

In 1875, Elisa Gray transmitted a few notes over telegraph wire and thought if you could send music then what next: voice, word.  The New York Times predicted the coming of a talking telegraph and the public grew eager for it.  Just one year later, Gray believed he had the answer, tin can voice chambers connected by a wire and a liquid that could turn vibrations into signals.  But he didn’t put his idea on paper for 2 months.  After finally making a sketch, he waited 4 more days before he went to the patent office.  When he arrived, Mr. Gray was told that a mere 2 hours earlier, a school teacher named Alexander Graham Bell bursted through the door with his own sketch.  Of course, you know the rest of the story….

 

Take action, get moving.

Don’t just generate ideas; do something.

title: Winston Churchill - Honor Everyone on The Team
content:
People who build successful teams never forget that every person's role is contributing to the bigger picture. One of the best examples of this is Winston Churchill. During World War II when Britain was experiencing its darkest days, the country had a difficult time keeping men working in the coal mines. Many wanted to give up their dirty, thankless jobs in the dangerous mines to join the military service, which got much public praise and support. Yet without coal, the military and the people at home would be in trouble.

So, Churchill faced thousands of coal miners one day and passionately told them of their importance to the war effort, and how their role could make or break the goal of maintaining England's freedom. It's said that tears appeared in the eyes of those hardened men. And they returned to their unglamorous work with steely resolve. That's the kind of mindset it takes to build a team.

title: Four Sons and Four Catholic Ladies
content:
I would like to start with something funny: I heard about these four Catholic ladies who were bragging about their sons. The first one said, My son is a priest; when he walks in the room, everyone calls him father.

The second said My son is a bishop; when he walks in the room, everyone calls him Your Grace.

The third said My son is a cardinal when he walks in the room, everyone calls him Your Eminence.

 

The fourth lady said, my son is six foot three, has broad shoulders, is incredibly good looking, dresses impeccably well, and when he walks in a room, all the ladies say, Oh my God.

title: 25th Wedding Anniversary
content: I heard about this elderly couple. They've been married for over 60 years. They were at a church fellowship, and someone asked them the secret of their success. The man told how he always treated his wife with respect and took her on trips all over the world. He said, in fact, for our 25th wedding anniversary, I took her to Beijing, China, and everyone politely applauded.  Then someone asked, What did you do for your 50th wedding anniversary. He said I went back and picked her up.

title: Adam and Eve
content: Adam said to God, why did you make Eve so beautiful? God said so you would love her. He said, why did you give her such long flowing hair?  God said it again so that you would love her. Well, God, why'd you give her such a great figure? God said the same thing so that you would love her. Adam said all right, God, you made her so beautiful, so attractive; why did you make her so dumb? God said that's easy, Adam, so that she would love you.

title: Baptist Man at Race Tracks
content:
I heard about this Baptist man named Bill. He liked to sneak out to the horse races and bet. One day, after losing almost all of his money, he saw a Catholic priest step out onto the tracks and bless a horse. Sure enough, that horse won first place. The next race. He blessed another horse, and that horse won again. Seeing this, Bill went down to the ATM machine and took out ALL of his money. This time, he saw the priest not only touch the horse’s forehead but his eyes, his ears, and all of his legs. Feeling competent, he bet all of his money, but in the middle of that race, the horse fell down dead. He couldn't believe it, he asked the priest, What in the world happened?

 

He said that's the problem with you Protestants; you don't know the difference between a blessing and the last rites.

title: Blonde Gets Pulled Over
content:
This is just a joke; don't be offended. But I heard about this blonde lady. She was driving down the freeway when she got pulled over by a female police officer, who also happened to be blond. The officer asked for her driver's license; she dug and dug in her purse, getting more and more agitated, couldn't find it, and finally asked the officer, What does it look like? She said it's a little square that has your picture on it. The lady found a mirror, saw herself in it, and handed it to the officer.

 

The Officer looked in the mirror and saw herself, handed it back, and said, You can go. I didn't realize you were a police officer.

title: Blonde Lady
content:
Let's start with something funny, and it’s just a joke; don't be offended.

 

I heard about this man, he was sitting in a dark restaurant, and he said to the lady sitting next to him. Would you like to hear a blonde joke? She said, wait before you tell me. You should know that I'm blonde, six feet tall, and a professional bodybuilder. The lady next to me is blonde, six foot two, and a professional wrestler. And the lady next to her is blonde six foot five, and the kickboxing champion of the world.

 

Now, do you still want to tell me? He thought about it a few moments, and no, not if I'm gonna have to explain it three times.

title: Burglar
content:
A little old lady surprised a burglar in her kitchen late one night. She was home alone, didn't have a weapon, she didn't know what she was going to do. She finally thought I’d quote a scripture verse; she shouted out ACTS 2:38; the burglar suddenly froze in his tracks and wouldn't move. Soon, the police arrived, and they were amazed that a woman with no weapon could do this. They asked the burglar what was it about that scripture that had such an effect on you.

 

He said scripture; I thought she said she had an axe and two 38s.

title: Checking The Red Light Camera
content:
I heard about this man; he was driving through an intersection that was monitored by cameras. If you ran the light or broke the law in any way, you'd receive a ticket in the mail. So he made sure to go through it extra slowly, but he noticed the camera flashed and took his picture. He thought that's not right. He turned around and drove through it even more slowly. Once again, the camera flashed, and he thought this thing was messed up. They could not give me a ticket out of spite, so he drove through it three more times, each time waving at the camera with a big smile.

A week later, he received five tickets in the mail for not wearing his seatbelt.

title: Clock
content:
I heard about this man who died and went to heaven. St Peter escorted him down this long hallway filled with clocks; the hands on the clocks were all moving at different speeds. Peter explained that every person has a clock. When they sin, the clock ticks. The man saw a clock barely moving; St Peter said that’s Billy Graham's clock. There was another clock creeping along, St. Peter said that’s  Mother Teresa's clock. He said curiously, can I see my clock?

 

St. Peter said yes, absolutely, we keep it in the office and use it as a fan.

title: Don’t Step on a Duck
content:
I like to start with something funny and I heard about these two ladies that died and went to heaven. St. Peter met them at the gate and said you'll be happy here. Suppose you follow one main rule. Don't step on a duck. If you step on a duck, they make a terrible racket. A week later, one of the ladies accidentally stepped on a duck. Peter came up to her with this extremely unattractive man. Nothing appealing about him whatsoever, said as your punishment, you're going to be chained to this man. Seeing this, the other lady was very careful. A month later, Peter came up to her with this incredibly handsome man. He has an amazing physique and looks like a movie star; he chained them together. The lady was thrilled.

 

She said to him, I can't believe I don't know what I did to deserve getting chained to you. He said, I don't know what you did, mamm, but I stepped on a duck.

title: Elderly Couple
content:
I heard about this elderly couple; they were sitting in a swing, celebrating their 60th wedding anniversary. Feeling romantic, the husband said to his wife, Honey, our love is tried and true. She had difficulty hearing it and asked him to repeat it. He said it louder. I said, Our love is tried and true. She still couldn't hear him and said, would you please speak up?

 

Frustrated, he shouted, I said, Our love is tried and true. She said, Well, fine. I'm sick of you, too.

title: Emergency Exit Only
content:
I was flying to an event with some colleagues on this very small plane, it would only hold a couple dozen people.  There was one seat on each side of the aisle.  After we took off I wanted to open my tray table so I could write some notes. The table was on the side of the plane, right underneath the window. I pulled and pulled, but I couldn’t get it open; it was stuck.

 

My friend was sitting across the aisle he pulled his straight out with no problem. I went back to mine, and I yanked and struggled.  I thought I was going to get this thing open if it’s the last thing that I do. My friend got up, came over, and he started pulling and pulling, and another staff member tried but it was stuck.  I just sat there, kind of frustrated.  Finally, I looked up and over the window where we had been pullingthere was a sign with big, bold letters; it said not a tray table, emergency exit only.

 

Oh boy, I didn’t laugh like some of you might want to laugh.

Anyway, sometimes, what we're frustrated about is God keeping us from real frustration.

 

In my case, it keeps me alive. (Being an emergency exit).

 

If God opened every door we asked him to open, answered every prayer we prayed, and brought every person we begged him to bring, we wouldn't reach our destiny. The longer I live, the easier it is for me to sleep when it doesn't work out my way. I may not understand it. It may not seem fair, but I've learned that God is smarter than I am.  He can see things we can't see, and he knows what he's doing.

 

I wonder if what's frustrating is that you has an emergency exit only sign on it and you can't see it. You don't understand why God won't answer the prayer, why the dream is taking so long. Why that guy at work that you like so much hasn't even noticed you. You've worn your best outfits, your best perfume, given him your best move, he acts like he's dead. Maybe it's because God can see something you can't see. Maybe under his shirt is an emergency exit only sign that's hidden from you.

 

God has your best interests at heart, he's not giving you what you want. That means he has something better. He loves you too much to let you miss your destiny.

title: Food Line
content:
There were 2 food lines in the cafeteria

  • At the beginning of line 1 was a basket of apples, a nun had written a note. It read, take only one God is watching.
  • At the beginning of line 2 was a box of chocolate chip cookies, a student had written, take all you want, God is watching the Apples.

title: Gifts for Mom
content:
Thought I start with something funny.

I heard about these three sons, who left home and went out and prospered; they got back together to talk about the gifts they bought their elderly mother. The first son said I built mom a big house. The second one said I got a fancy car. The third son said since mom loves to read the Bible, she can barely see anymore. I got her a specially trained parrot that can quote the entire Bible. A few months later, they received a letter from their mother. It said Milton, the house you built me is way too big, Terrel on the car you bought me is way too small, but my dearest Don, your simple gift is my favorite. The chicken was delicious.

Some people have to learn the importance of asking questions the hard way!

 

Millions saw the Apple fall, but Newton was the one who asked why!

title: God’s Secret Service
content:
I heard about this pastor, he was in the lobby after service greeting people and he saw this man that he hadn't seen in a long long time, he pulled him over to the side and said, Sir, you need to join the army of the Lord. The man said what are you talking about, I'm in the army of the Lord.  Pastor said, Well, how come I only see you on Christmas and Easter?

He whispered back, I'm in the Secret Service.

title: Groceries from the Devil
content:
I like to start with something funny I heard about this country grandmother, she'd go out on her front porch every morning and thank the Lord for another day. Her neighbor didn't believe in God. He'd shout back there's no such thing as the Lord. One day, he overheard her asking God to give her groceries for the week, he snuck over the next morning and put some groceries on the front porch, she got up and said thank you, Lord, You did it again. Her neighbor laughed and laughed and said God didn't give you those groceries, I put them there.

 

She said, Lord, thank you, you not only gave me the groceries, but you made the devil pay for it.

title: Hearing Aid
content:
I heard about this elderly man, who had a serious hearing problem for many years. He went to the doctor and was fitted with his new high-tech, state-of-the-art hearing aid to wear. He could hear 100%. A month later he came back to the doctor for a checkup. The doctor said wow your hearing is perfect your family must be so excited that you can hear again.

He said no, I haven't told my family. I just sit around listening to the different conversations and I've changed my will three times.

title: Lady Complaining to God
content:
I read about a lady who was complaining about everything that went wrong that day. She said God, why did you let so many bad things happen to me today.  My alarm didn’t go off, so I was late to work,  at lunch they made the wrong sandwich and I had to send it back. Driving home, my cell phone dropped the call right in the middle of a conversation. To top it off, when I got home, I wanted to put my feet in the foot massager but it wouldn’t turn on, nothing went right today.

 

God said, all right let me go down the list, Your alarm didn’t go off because there was a drunk driver on the road, I delayed you on purpose so you wouldn’t be harmed.  About your sandwich, that lady wasn’t feeling well and I didn’t want you to catch what they had, so I had someone else fix it. And on that dropped call on the way home that person was about to fill you with gossip and I didn’t want you to be contaminated, so I cut it off.  And that foot massager, it had a short in it, if you had turned it on it would have knocked out the power and I didn’t think you wanted to sit around in the dark all night.

 

Could it be that what’s frustrating you is really the hand of God? Could he be behind the scenes doing things you can’t see but it’s for your good? He’s protecting you, guiding you, positioning you. Nothing happens without God’s permission we’re not always going to understand it.

title: Living at Rest
content:
I heard about this church service one Sunday morning. Everything was going great until a bolt of lightning hit the sanctuary. When the smoke cleared, Satan himself was standing at the podium. People panicked and took off running as fast as they could. Everyone, that is, except one lady. She sat in the front row just as calm as can be. Satan was appalled, he said lady, Do you know who I am? She said I sure do. He said, aren't you afraid of me?

She said, Not in the least bit. He said why not? She said, Why should I be? I’ve been married to your brother for 30 years.

title: One Parachute Left
content:
I heard about this airplane, that was about to crash. There were four passengers but only three parachutes. The first passenger said I'm a leading heart surgeon, my patients need me, he took the first parachute and jumped. The second passenger said, I'm a rocket scientist, one of the smartest men alive My country needs me, he took the second parachute and jumped. The third passenger was Pope John Paul, he said to the fourth passenger a 10-year-old boy scout. I'm old and frail, I don't have much time left you can have the last parachute.

The boy scout said don't worry about it, sir. There are still two parachutes left, you see the smartest man alive, he just jumped out with my backpack.

title: Texas gone wireless
content:
I heard about this archaeologist in New York. He dug down 10 feet and found traces of copper wiring, dating back 100 years, he concluded that New Yorkers had a telephone network over 100 years ago. Not to be outdone, an archaeologist from California down 20 feet and found copper wiring dating back 200 years. He concluded that California had a massive communications network 100 years earlier than New Yorkers.

Upon hearing this, Bubba from Texas dug down 30 feet on his farm and found absolutely nothing. He concluded 300 years ago, Texans had already gone wireless.

title: The Enemy Can Help
content:
I heard about this elderly lady who was at the store and she accidentally locked her keys in her car. She was using a coat hanger, to try to get it open with no success. She prayed and asked God to help her. About this time, this really rough-looking guy drove up on a motorcycle wearing a leather jacket,  tattoos, and a skullcap, in 15 seconds, he had a car door open. She hugged him and said, Lord, thank you for sending me this nice man.

He said lady, I'm not a nice man. I just got out of prison for auto theft. She gave him a big hug and say Lord thank you, you even sent me a professional.

title: There was a man sitting
content:
There was a man sitting and reading the newspaper when all of a sudden his wife hit him aside the head.

He turned and asked, “Why did you do that?”

His wife said I just found this note in your pocket with the name Mary Lou on it. He said, “Oh honey that is a horse I bet on today.”  She said oh.

Well, a few days later, she hit him aside the head again. He asked, “Now why did you do that.”

 

His wife looked at him and said, “That’s for the phone call I received from your horse today.”

title: Understand women or build a bridge.
content:
I heard about this man that was walking on the beach. God said, Son, you've been so faithful. I'm going to grant you one special wish, the man was so excited.

He said, God, I've always wanted to go to Hawaii, but I'm afraid to fly. So my wish is that you would build me a bridge across the ocean. God said, Son, that's totally impossible. Think of the logistics of that, take some time, and wish again.

He said okay God, I've been married four times, all my ex-wives say I am so insensitive. So my wish is that I would be able to understand a woman. I want to know why they think like they think, why they feel like they feel.

 

There was a long pause, God said, Do you want two lanes or four lanes on that bridge?

title: Water to Wine
content:
I heard about this minister, he was driving down the road when he got pulled over by a policeman. The officer came up to the window and smelled alcohol. He saw a thermos and said, Sir, what are you drinking? The minister said just water officer.

He asked to see the thermos and he took one sniff and said, smells like wine to me. The minister said what do you know, Jesus did it again.

title: Wife is Broke
content:
I heard about this husband who died. He left his wife $20,000. After the funeral, his wife told a friend that she was totally broke. Her friend asked, what do you mean you’re broke, I thought you said you had $20,000. She said, well I spent $5,000 on the funeral and $15,000 on the memorial stone.

Her friend said, wow that has to be some kind of stone. How big was it? She held up her finger and said three and a half karats.

title: Louisiana boy goes to college
content:
An old Louisiana boy from deep in the swamp went off to college.

The college was too far away from the young student to go back home often, so his grandfather told him to just stay there.

As it got closer to the holidays, the young man wrote a letter to his grandfather and told him it would be more expensive for him to stay on campus during the holiday rather than go home for Christmas.

His grandfather couldn’t read or write, so he would always get someone else to read the letter to him.  Then they wrote the grandson back and said, “Come home for Christmas since it would be cheaper.”

The local town got together and made a big meal for the young man’s return.

When he got home for the holiday his grandfather asked him what did he learn.  He said, tell me something, anything you learn.  The young man was resistant at first and told his grandfather you won’t understand it.

The grandfather said, “Boy, you better tell me something you learned.”

So, he said, ok, I’ll tell you some Algebra.  His grandpa said, ok great tell me some Algebra.

 

The boy said pi are square.

His grandfather looked at him and said, “You have been gone all this time and that’s what you learned.”  He said, all this and that’s it. Boy, you don’t know nothing.   Everybody knows that pi are round and cornbread are square.

 

Tribute to Justin Wilson, the cajun cook

title: Louisiana cajun twin horses
content:
Old Cajun boy was educated in I think MS, I guarantee it wasn’t in Louisiana.

Old cajun had twin horses, which is rare.  He would always say, I can never tell these horses apart.

 

One of his friends went to help him figure out how to tell the horses apart.

He said, let’s measure them.  The old cajun said, I’ve tried that to but they are the same.  He said they are both 15.5’ high on the dot, so we can’t tell a difference from that.

 

His friend said, well have you thought trimming the tail.  He said, yes, I thought of that but the darn tail grows back every time.

 

His friend asked him, did you measure how long they are?  He said, no I never thought about that.  He said, well let’s measure them.  One of them was exactly 3/4 of a hand longer than the other one.

 

He said, see, that was easy, now you can tell the difference.  One of them is 3/4-hand longer than the other, now you can tell real quick.

 

He said, you know, I always thought that black horse was longer than that white horse.

 

Tribute to Justin Wilson, the Cajun cook

title: Louisiana drunk driver & preacher
content:
Down in this little town in South Louisiana, they finally built a new 4-lane highway and a couple of new stoplights.  I have a friend who was driving on that highway, he wasn’t totally drunk, he just felt like driving across all 4 lanes, and driving right behind him was a preacher friend of ours.  The preacher was concerned because my friend was swerving all over the road and he couldn’t get around him.

My lightly drunk friend lit a cigarette and the car straightened itself up.  The preacher was then able to pass right around him.  By this time, the preacher was concerned about it as he was watching him in his rearview mirror.  In fact, he was watching him too good in the mirror because the road turned but the preacher didn’t.  He ran straight into an old Live Oak Tree and tore his car up.  I mean, tore it up.

My friend makes it up close to where the preacher was.  He struggled out of his car and as he did that the preacher struggled out of his car too.  My friend asked him, “Are you hurt my friend, the preacher said no, I’m good.” My friend said you are lucky, to tear your car up like that and not a scratch you don’t realize how lucky you are.  Well, you know the preacher didn’t believe in luck, so he said, “No, I’m blessed, the Lord was with me and saved me.”

My drunk friend said, well the way you drive you better let him ride with me because if you don’t, you gonna kill him.

 

Tribute to Justin Wilson, the Cajun cook

title: Louisiana friends
content:
Two of my uncles were sharing a garden with each other.  They also had one mule that they shared. One week it was raining all “get up” out there.  They kept looking out the window and seeing their poor little mule in that rain.   One of my uncles said we should build a stable for that mule because if he stays out in that rain like that, he could catch pneumonia and we can’t afford that.  You know, a good mule that you train to plow is hard to get.  My other uncle said yes, you are correct.  Let’s build one.

 

They said ok, as soon as it stops raining let’s build one. So, they waited until it stopped raining and built a stable.  My uncle said, let me go get the mule.  He got the rope put it on the mules’ neck and walked him up to the door of the stable.  They built the door entry real low, as they tried to walk in, the mule’s ears hit the top and he backed off.  One of them said, look at that, the mule’s ears are too long for the door.  We are gonna have to cut the mule’s ears.  So they got the straight razor and grease to cut the mule’s ears.  As they were trying to hold the mule still to cut his ears, one of their nephews walked up.  The nephew asked, what are y’all doing?  The old man said, this mule’s ears is too long to go in the door, so we gonna cut his ears to go in there.

 

His nephew said, well all you have to do is dig a hole so he can go in there.  They said, well thank you very much, then the nephew walked off.  The uncle says, that’s a good boy.  He’s been at Mississippi State for 4 years now and they done taught him.  But I guarantee you, you don’t have a dig a whole to trim a mule’s ears.

 

Communication is critical to make sure everybody is on the same page.

You have to communicate with people where they are.

 

Tribute to Justin Wilson, the Cajun cook

title: Louisiana - Shallow water
content:
Down in south Louisiana, we love to fish. This old cajun boy was on the banks of the bayou fishing and an old cattleman walked up and asked, “Do you know a shallow place on this bayou where I can cross with my horse?”  The fisherman said yes, but why do you want to cross?  The cattleman said I have some cows on the other side that I need to round up.

 

The fisherman told him to go right down there and it’s real shallow.  So, the cattleman grabbed his horse and walked down the bank then started to go across.  Splash, he and his horse went straight under the water, all you could see was his hat floating. When he finally came back up, he yelled to the fisherman why you lied to me that this area was shallow?

 

The fisherman yelled back, I didn’t lie to you.  He yelled back oh yes you did and when I get out of here, I’m gonna whip you.  The fisherman said no I didn’t. He said yes you did.

 

The fisherman said no I didn’t. He said just a few minutes before you crossed there, there was a lil duck with 2” short legs crossed right there without any problem.

 

Tribute to Justin Wilson, the Cajun cook

title: Ants Fighting
content:
If you collect 100 black ants and 100 red ants and put them in a glass jar, nothing will happen, but if you take the jar, shake it violently, and leave it on the table, the ants will start killing each other. Reds believe that black is the enemy, while black believes that red is the enemy when the real enemy is the person who shook the jar.

 

The same is true in society.

Men vs Women

Left vs Right

Rich vs poor

Faith vs Science

Gossip, rumors, etc ...

 

Before we fight each other, we must ask ourselves:

Who rocked the jar?

Who told you that?

Why did you believe that?

Why didn’t you talk to me first?
